ZF's Commercial Vehicle Solutions (CVS) division helps shaping the future of commercial transportation ecosystems.  Why you should choose ZF in India:

 Be part of our ZF team as Assistant Manager - Manufacturing Engineering (Tool design) and apply now!

 Contact

jobs.title: Industrialization Engineer
jobs.desc:
At Alstom, we understand transport networks and what moves people. From high-speed trains, metros, monorails, and trams, to turnkey systems, services, infrastructure, signalling, and digital mobility, we offer our diverse customers the broadest portfolio in the industry. Every day, 80,000 colleagues lead the way to greener and smarter mobility worldwide, connecting cities as we reduce carbon and replace cars.

 Could you be the full-time Industrialization Engineer in Duhai/Modipuram we’re looking for?
 Your future role 

 Take on a new challenge and apply your industrial engineering expertise in a cutting-edge field. You’ll work alongside collaborative, innovative, and detail-oriented teammates.

 You'll play a key role in supporting industrial activities at Duhai/Modipuram depots as part of the RRTS Project’s 15-year service contract. Day-to-day, you’ll work closely with teams across the business (Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Sourcing, and EHS), create and implement industrial processes, and collaborate with external subcontractors, suppliers, and customers.

 You’ll specifically take care of creating standard operation processes and work instructions, but also support the implementation of IS tools like GSI/SES and customer interfaces for GSI/Maximo.

 We’ll look to you for:

• 
 Developing and maintaining standard operation processes and work instructions, including EHS and railway safety actions, parts and tools lists, and traceability records

• 
 Supporting the implementation of IS tools (e.g., GSI/SES) and customer interface for GSI/Maximo

• 
 Verifying the list of parts for maintenance, including local technical information and supplier requirements

• 
 Creating PM plan trackers, including work instructions, material, BOM, lifting plans, tooling, and fixtures

• 
 Participating in the design of material handling equipment (MHE) and specific tooling

• 
 Ensuring the maintenance of industrial equipment and managing active tools on-site and at subcontractors

• 
 Managing industrial activities, including e-buy creation, supplier follow-up, and internal coordination

• 
 Documenting the list and location of machines, infrastructure equipment, jigs, and tools

 All about you 

 We value passion and attitude over experience. That’s why we don’t expect you to have every single skill. Instead, we’ve listed some that we think will help you succeed and grow in this role:

• 
 Degree in Mechanical or Electrical Engineering (BE/B.Tech)

• 
 Strong hands-on experience in SAP PM module end-to-end processes, Maximo, and Qlik Sense

• 
 Knowledge of middleware functionality

• 
 Experience in rolling stock maintenance

• 
 5 years of experience in rolling stock, project management, or equivalent

• 
 Competency in process and method development

• 
 Proficiency in CAD, 3D tools, and SAP

• 
 Excellent communication, collaboration, and teaching skills

• 
 Autonomous, rigorous, and innovative mindset

• 
 Proficiency in English (reading, writing, and speaking)

 Things you’ll enjoy Join us on a life-long transformative journey – the rail industry is here to stay, so you can grow and develop new skills and experiences throughout your career. You’ll also:

• 
 Enjoy stability, challenges, and a long-term career free from boring daily routines

• 
 Work with new security standards for rail signalling

• 
 Collaborate with transverse teams and helpful colleagues

• 
 Contribute to innovative projects

• 
 Utilise our dynamic and inclusive working environment

• 
 Steer your career in whatever direction you choose across functions and countries

• 
 Benefit from our investment in your development through award-winning learning

• 
 Progress towards leadership or specialized technical roles

• 
 Benefit from a fair and dynamic reward package that recognises your performance and potential, plus comprehensive and competitive social coverage (life, medical, pension)

 You don’t need to be a train enthusiast to thrive with us. We guarantee that when you step onto one of our trains with your friends or family, you’ll be proud. If you’re up for the challenge, we’d love to hear from you!

 Important to note 

 As a global business, we’re an equal-opportunity employer that celebrates diversity across the 63  countries we operate in. We’re committed to creating an inclusive workplace for everyone.

jobs.title: Mechanical Design (Gas turbine parts in general)
jobs.desc:
Mechanical Design Engineer will be responsible for the design of the gas turbine components including compressors, turbines, shafts, bearing systems, and stationary structures within the turbojet and turbofan development programs. This role requires expert knowledge in mechanical design, integrity, gas turbine propulsion, planning for projects and ability to develop individuals. 

Key Responsibilities: 
• Design and optimize the gas turbine static and rotary systems for life, weight, manufacturability and cost. 
• Carry out Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerancing tasks, define assembly procedures. 
• Prepare drawings and define manufacturing guidelines 
• Carry out FMECA (Failure Mode, Effects, and Criticality Analysis) to support the safety and operability assessments 
• Support other team members, develop junior engineers and provide constructive feedback 
• Review the designs, simulations and generate testing guidelines 
• Identify project risks and plan for mitigation 

Qualifications & Experience: 
• Aerospace, Mechanical Engineering degree or a related field. 
• Strong background in gas turbine propulsion, mechanical design, integrity and heat transfer. 
• Fluent in English 
• Experience: 5-15 years or more. 
• Experience in one or a combination of the activities, not limited to o Design of gas turbine externals and accessories i.e., fuel pump, oil pump, bleed lines. o Design and sizing of disks, shafts, couplings, connection elements. 
o Design and sizing of accessory gearbox, shaft power off-take o FRACAS (Failure Reporting, Analysis, & Corrective Action System) activities. 

Skills: 
• Technical skills in one or a combination of stated topics. 
• Proficient in one of design packages such as Solidworks, Siemens NX or similar. 
• Experience in PLM tools such as Teamcenter, Windchill or similar. 
• Experience in FEA, or lower order simulation methods. 
• Experience in programming using C, Matlab/Simulink or similar. 
• Awareness on the state-of-the-art technologies in materials, aerodynamics, and structural mechanics to link with mechanical design for gas turbine propulsion 
• Good communication and presentation skills to interact with team members, clients, and vendors. 
• Ability to solve problems, prioritize tasks and delegate when necessary

jobs.desc:

If you seek to make a difference on a global scale, working with next-gen technologies and the sharpest collaborative teams, then we could be a perfect match. 
 What you will do 

 Responsible for developing, industrializing, stabilizing and continuously improving BIW manufacturing processes for truck cabs, ensuring safety, quality, productivity, cost competitiveness and timely delivery of new products.

 The role will work closely with Product Engineering, Production, Quality, Maintenance, Tooling, Automation, Industrial Engineering and Suppliers to establish robust BIW processes from concept through SOP and volume production.

 Key Responsibilities 

 BIW Process Engineering 

• Develop manufacturing processes and operation sequences for truck cab BIW.

• Define welding, joining, assembly and inspection processes.

• Prepare and maintain Process Flow, PFMEA, Control Plan and Standard Work.

• Establish optimum process parameters and ensure process capability.

• Identify and eliminate process bottlenecks and sources of variation.

 BIW Welding & Joining 

• Develop and optimize spot welding, MIG welding, stud welding, riveting and other joining processes.

• Define welding parameters and ensure consistent weld quality.

• Resolve welding defects such as missing welds, spatter, burn-through, distortion and weak welds.

• Improve welding productivity, quality and process reliability.

 Fixtures, Tooling & Equipment 

• Develop concepts and specifications for BIW fixtures, jigs, gauges and tooling.

• Review fixture designs for datum strategy, locating, clamping, accessibility, ergonomics and fool-proofing.

• Participate in tooling design reviews, trials, buy-off and commissioning.

• Ensure tooling capability meets dimensional and production requirements.

 Industrialization & Continuous Improvement 

 New Product Introduction / Industrialization 

• Lead BIW manufacturing activities for new truck/cab programs.

• Review product designs with  manufacturability perspectives.

• Coordinate prototype, pilot and pre-production builds.

• Lead tooling and equipment readiness activities.

• Ensure BIW manufacturing readiness against project milestones.

• Support successful SOP and production ramp-up.

 Automation & Industry 4.0 

• Identify opportunities for automation and semi-automation.

• Support implementation of:

• Robotic welding

• Automated material handling

• Vision systems

• Sensors and process monitoring

• Error-proofing / Poka-Yoke

• Traceability systems

• Drive digitalization and data-based process improvement.

 Productivity & Continuous Improvement 

 Drive improvements in: 

• Cycle time study

• Line balancing

• Process efficiency

• Energy consumption

• Process reliability

 Apply Lean Manufacturing, Kaizen, VSM, TPM and structured problem-solving to eliminate waste and improve process performance. 

 Production & Quality Support 

• Provide technical support to BIW production for daily manufacturing issues.

• Resolve chronic process and dimensional problems.

• Conduct shop-floor process audits.

• Ensure adherence to standard processes and parameters.

• Drive reduction in welding defects, dimensional defects, rework and scrap.

• Support internal/customer quality audits.

• Implement effective Poka-Yoke and process controls.

 Supplier & Project Management 

• Coordinate with fixture, tooling, automation and equipment suppliers.

• Review supplier technical proposals and designs.

• Participate in FAT, SAT, trials and commissioning.

• Monitor supplier activities against project milestones.

• Ensure timely delivery of tooling and process equipment.

 Competencies & skills 

 Technical Competencies 

 Essential: 

• BIW manufacturing and assembly processes

• Truck cab / sheet-metal manufacturing

• Spot and MIG welding

• BIW fixtures, jigs, gauges and tooling

• GD&T and dimensional control

• BIW geometry and variation management

• PFMEA, Control Plan and Process Flow

• Root Cause Analysis

• Line balancing and capacity planning

• Lean Manufacturing / Kaizen

• Robotic welding and automation

• Industry 4.0 / smart manufacturing

• CAD interpretation – CATIA / NX / AutoCAD

jobs.title: Ingénieur - Outillage spécialisé et équipement de diagnostique
jobs.desc:
Req ID:521771 

 Chez Alstom, nous avons une connaissance pointue des réseaux de transport et comprenons ce qui conduit les individus à les emprunter. Des trains à grande vitesse, métros, monorails et tramways aux systèmes intégrés, services, infrastructures, et solutions de signalisation et de mobilité numérique, nous offrons à la diversité de nos clients le portefeuille le plus vaste du secteur.  Chaque jour, plus de 80 000 collaborateurs dans le monde qui ouvrent la voie à des solutions de mobilité plus vertes et plus intelligentes pour relier les villes, réduire l’empreinte carbone et remplacer la voiture.

 Notre organisation, le milieu ferroviaire, nos projets vous attirent, nous avons un poste qui pourrait vous intéresser.

 Pourriez-vous être le/la  Ingénieur(e) – Outillages spéciaux et équipements de diagnostic et d’essais sur banc à temps plein à Saint-Bruno que nous recherchons?

 Votre futur rôle 

 Relevez un nouveau défi et mettez à profit votre expertise en génie mécanique dans un environnement ferroviaire à la fine pointe de la technologie. Vous travaillerez aux côtés de collègues passionnés, collaboratifs et innovants.

 Dans ce rôle, au sein de l’équipe  Integrated Services Readiness (ISR) , vous serez responsable du suivi complet des livrables clients liés aux outillages de maintenance spéciaux et aux équipements de diagnostic, de la conception jusqu’à la livraison. Vous veillerez à ce que tous les livrables soient remis dans les délais prescrits et répondent pleinement aux exigences des clients.

 Principales responsabilités 

• Analyser les spécifications techniques des clients afin d’identifier les exigences relatives aux outillages de maintenance spéciaux et aux équipements de diagnostic.

• Évaluer les propositions techniques des fournisseurs.

• Examiner et approuver les dossiers techniques soumis par les fournisseurs, y compris les dessins et les descriptions techniques.

• Participer aux revues de conception avec les fournisseurs et les clients.

• Assurer le suivi de la fabrication et de la livraison des équipements.

• Soutenir les activités d’installation et de mise en service chez les clients.

• Planifier et coordonner les activités techniques liées aux équipements sous votre responsabilité.

• Examiner et approuver les procédures d’essais servant à valider la conception des équipements.

• Participer aux essais de qualification réalisés chez les fournisseurs.

• Concevoir des équipements de diagnostic de maintenance ainsi que des outillages de maintenance spécialisés.

 À propos de vous 

 Nous valorisons autant la passion et l’attitude que l’expérience. C’est pourquoi nous ne nous attendons pas à ce que vous possédiez toutes les compétences recherchées. Voici celles qui, selon nous, vous aideront à réussir et à évoluer dans ce rôle :

• Baccalauréat en génie mécanique .

• Diplôme d’études collégiales (DEC) en technologie du génie mécanique (un atout).

• Minimum de 5 ans d’expérience pertinente en ingénierie.

• Maîtrise de CATIA V5 pour la conception et la réalisation de dessins d’outillages de maintenance.

• Connaissance des essais d’équipements électromécaniques, hydrauliques et pneumatiques.

• Excellentes habiletés de communication en français et en anglais. 

• Membre/Eligible OIQ  

 Ce que vous apprécierez 

 L’industrie ferroviaire est là pour rester, vous permettant de développer continuellement de nouvelles compétences et d’acquérir diverses expériences tout au long de votre carrière.

 De plus, vous aurez l’occasion de :

• Intégrer un leader mondial de la mobilité durable.

• Travailler sur des projets ferroviaires novateurs ayant une portée internationale.

• Collaborer avec des équipes multidisciplinaires et des experts de l’industrie.

• Profiter d’opportunités d’évolution professionnelle au sein d’une organisation diversifiée et inclusive.

• Contribuer à l’avenir du transport et à des solutions de mobilité plus vertes.

• Bénéficier dès votre premier jour d’un programme de rémunération équitable et dynamique qui reconnaît votre performance et votre potentiel, ainsi que d’un régime complet et concurrentiel d’avantages sociaux (assurance vie, assurance médicale et régime de retraite).

 Nul besoin d’être passionné(e) de trains pour vous épanouir chez nous.

 Nous vous garantissons que lorsque vous monterez à bord de l’un de nos trains avec votre famille ou vos amis, vous en serez fier(ère). Si vous êtes prêt(e) à relever le défi, nous aimerions faire votre connaissance!

 Remarque importante 

 En tant qu’employeur présent dans plus de 63 pays, nous souscrivons au principe d’égalité d’accès à l’emploi et valorisons la diversité. Nous nous sommes engagés à créer un environnement de travail inclusif pour tous.

 Assist Program Managers in providing technical and administrative support for new program launches and current production operations for tools and dies used in the manufacturing of stamped metal components and assemblies.

 MINIMUM JOB REQUIREMENTS: 
 • Tool and Die Maker with minimum 5 years’ experience beyond completion of formal apprenticeship.

 • Support new business quotes with part feasibilities, and costing; be able to calculate coil strip widths and feed lengths, set number of stations required, estimate tonnage requirements, run and interpret stamping simulations, and formulate detailed RFQs.

jobs.desc:
Transport is at the core of modern society. Imagine using your expertise to shape sustainable transport and infrastructure solutions for the future. If you seek to make a difference on a global scale, working with next-gen technologies and the sharpest collaborative teams, then we could be a perfect match. 

 Project Description 

 The Volvo Trucks Plant in Tuve, Gothenburg, produces heavy trucks for the global market. Since Tuve is the introduction plant for Volvo Trucks we are the first to produce new models of our vehicles. Therefore, most new process tools are designed in Tuve and then copied to other assembly plants.

 The Tooling & Equipment department receives work orders through a SharePoint based system and now there is a wish to find a more modern and efficient solution.

 Task :

SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

 TOOLING ENGINEER, AI SATELLITES (STARMIND) 

 SpaceX is leveraging its experience deploying and operating the world’s largest satellite constellation to develop Starmind, a new constellation of satellites capturing solar energy in space to power low-cost, high-performance AI compute for Earth. Realizing this vision demands highly reliable, high performance electrical compute hardware, solar power systems, thermal radiators, and more. These systems must operate in the extreme environment of space while delivering the connectivity, control, power distribution, and processing needed for orbital AI inference. 

 The Starmind team designs, builds, and operates the orbital compute fabric of the future. We develop nearly every key piece of technology in house – from the satellites’ flight computers and power systems to the fully custom compute electronics, memory, and networking that form the brain of our on-orbit data centers. As a Tooling Engineer on the Starmind team, you’ll have ownership over the entire manufacturing line for the hardware that enables advanced on-orbit AI processing and data center workloads. Your work spans the assembly, integration, and testing of industry-leading compute electronics, memory, and networking in order to achieve required domain sizes and processing workloads. 

 RESPONSIBILITIES: 

• Develop machining capability in-house for the tool & die team and deliver high-quality precision piece parts required to build internal tooling 

• Analyze piece parts and assemblies for DFM to ensure that the parts are optimized for manufacturing and assembly 

• Create collaborative business plans with design engineering, upstream production, and support teams and develop and maintain positive supplier/customer relationships 

• Work between manufacturing and design engineers, machinists, technicians, and quality personnel to ensure processes are robust and any production problems are quickly solved 

• Implement machining process controls that allow parts to run ‘lights out’. Leverage latest technologies and programming strategies to reduce in-cycle intervention 

• Identify, recommend, procure, and install machine shop equipment as well as ensure all equipment is thoroughly maintained and calibrated 

• Responsible for cost optimization and cost reduction initiatives associated with fabrication and processes 

• Continually develop and manage engineering capacity, schedules, and project plans in order to support production manifest as well as a diverse and variable R&D demand 

• Research and identify new materials, manufacturing technologies and finishing options 

• Inform estimations of prototype and production manufacturing costs - tooling, secondary assembly, secondary finishing and piece part 

• Publish and maintain detailed schedules for each development project segment 

 BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: 

• Bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline

 SpaceX is seeking a Tooling Designer for High Pressure Die Casting, to own the design and development of die casting tools and trim dies used to produce casted components. Transformer notre système industriel. Vous aurez la responsabilité de développer et de mettre en œuvre des solutions d'outillage innovantes et compétitives pour réduire nos coûts récurrents (RC) tout en minimisant notre empreinte environnementale.

 En tant que garant de la performance de nos systèmes industriels composites, vous piloterez les activités suivantes :
 • Ingénierie de Développement : Définir et valider la faisabilité de nouveaux processus via des technologies composites matures et robustes (RTM, pré-imprégnés, drapage).
• Design to Cost & Manufacturing : Challenger la conception en collaboration avec les experts métiers, architectes et ingénieurs systèmes (ISE) pour optimiser les performances et la qualité.
• Pilotage de l'Outillage : Superviser la création d'outillages complexes (moules d'injection, outils d'usinage/détourage, lignes d'assemblage) en matériaux variés (Acier, Invar, Alu, Composite).
• Transformation Numérique : Sécuriser l'intégration de l'automatisation et des outils digitaux dans le futur système industriel.
• Management & Gestion : Encadrer une petite équipe, piloter les budgets de développement et gérer les contrats de prestations de services.

 🛠️ Votre profil (Ce qui fera la différence)  
 Vous justifiez d'au moins 5 ans d'expérience sur un poste similaire.
Vous êtes doté d'une vision stratégique, capable de naviguer entre le bureau d'études (Avant-projets) et les réalités du terrain industriel.
 Compétences Techniques (Hard Skills) : 
 • Expertise Matériaux : Maîtrise des procédés composites (Thermodurcissables/Époxy et Thermoplastiques) et des matériaux métalliques associés (Invar, Acier).

 Qualités recherchées (Soft Skills) : Vous faites preuve d’une grande curiosité intellectuelle et de créativité pour imaginer les solutions de demain. Votre rigueur et votre méthodologie vous permettent de mener à bien des projets complexes en équipe, tout en restant polyvalent et mobile.

jobs.desc:

 What we offer: 
 At Magna, you can expect an engaging and dynamic environment where you can help to develop industry-leading automotive technologies. We invest in our employees, providing them with the support and resources they need to succeed. As a member of our global team, you can expect exciting, varied responsibilities as well as a wide range of development prospects. Because we believe that your career path should be as unique as you are.

 Group Summary: 
 The Magna Exteriors portfolio of products includes access systems such as liftgates, exterior trim, modular systems, front-end modules including fascia, active aerodynamic systems and other lightweight structural components for automotive, commercial truck and other industrial markets.
 Recognized globally as an innovator in all aspects of vehicle exteriors, Magna provides everything needed, from materials development and design through manufacturing and assembly, to help automakers create sleek, state-of-the-art vehicles across the world.

 Job Responsibilities: 

 JOB SUMMARY: 
 The Tool Engineer at Magna Engineered Glass is responsible for leading the technical development, procurement, validation, and continuous improvement of tooling used in the manufacture of encapsulated glass automotive windows. This role ensures all tooling (prototype, soft-tool, and production) is designed, built, sampled, and approved in compliance with Magna, customer, regulatory, and safety standards. The position requires specialized expertise in injection molding of encapsulated glass, including mold design, material behavior, glass loading, adhesion performance, sealing, and overmold processes. 
 The Tool Engineer collaborates with Product Engineering, Program Management, Supplier Quality, Manufacturing Engineering, and Tooling Suppliers (domestic and international) to ensure world class tool builds, robust manufacturability, and flawless launch execution. 
 JOB RESPONSIBILITIES:` 
 • Tooling Development & Standards • Maintain and apply corporate tooling standards for injection molded encapsulation tools. 
• Identify, evaluate, and maintain qualified tooling suppliers with demonstrated capability in encapsulated glass molding, including vertical presses, robot assisted glass loading, and automated demold. 
• Develop and validate new tooling processes including: • Encapsulation overmold of automotive glass 
• Dynamic pressure pad systems 
• Magnetized bezel or stiffener insert molding 
• Soft seal tooling and integrated glass fixturing systems 

• Lead mold design reviews; verify parting lines, gating, runner systems (hot & cold), steel selection, shrink rates, cooling strategy, and texturing requirements. • Ensure tool designs incorporate requirements for glass edge protection, dimensional stability, adhesion performance, and sealing surfaces. 
• Maintain complete data retention: 2D/3D tool designs, CMM reports, process sheets, hot runner data, and material/manifold documentation. 

• Manufacturability & Product Integration • Evaluate new product quotes for feasibility of glass encapsulation molding, including: • Glass edge tolerances and flatness 
• Cross section design for seals, beads, and retention features 
• Adhesion and overmold bonding requirements 
• Gate location impact on flow induced stresses in glass and polymer 

• Collaborate with Designers, Program Managers, Tooling Suppliers, and Project Engineers to ensure product design supports robust encapsulation manufacturability. • Participate in product design reviews to confirm draft, shut offs, retention geometry, gaging datums, and warp/shrink predictions meet customer specifications. 

• Tool Build Management & Launch • Prepare, manage, and approve tooling quotes for encapsulation tools within the corporate system. 
• Track tool builds through timing plans, supplier visits, milestone reviews, and PPAP readiness. 
• Lead sampling and launch of new tools including: • Glass loading validation 
• Overmold sealing performance 
• Adhesion / peel testing 
• Tool debug for short shots, flash, sinks, voids, and stress marks 

• Validate tooling and equipment through CMM layout, glass fixture verification, and encapsulation profile conformance. 
• Oversee texture (grain) approvals and surface quality reviews. 
• Define and release spare parts, preventive maintenance plans, and critical spare steel. 
• Support packaging, racking, and gage design reviews. 

• Analysis, Testing & Supplier Interaction • Direct Mold Flow and CAE studies specific to encapsulated glass: • Flow front around glass substrate 
• Knit line and adhesion risk areas 
• Cooling of non uniform wall sections 
• Polymer stress transfer into glass edges 

• Maintain material line cards including TPE, PVC, PC/ABS, TPU, and specialty encapsulation compounds. 
• Support supplier tool builds, including on site assessments of mold design, machining quality, tryout equipment, and process capability. 
• Support component and system testing including: • Glass adhesion pull tests 
• Weathering & UV durability 
• Thermal cycling and expansion mismatch evaluation 

• Troubleshoot issues for existing programs (e.g., de lamination, glass cracking, warp, dimension failures). 
• Participate in formal supplier evaluations after project completion. 

• Documentation & Reporting • Document all technical decisions, tool modifications, sampling results, and validation activities. 
• Maintain accurate, updated timing charts and project status for all assigned tools. 
• Prepare cost reports, variance analyses, and support budgeting and forecast activities. 

• Process & Continuous Improvement • Maintain expertise in emerging encapsulation tool technologies, such as: • Advanced hot runner systems for hybrid materials 
• Tool steel performance for glass contact areas 
• Adhesion promoting surface treatments

jobs.desc:
When applicable, Bombardier promotes flexible and hybrid work policies. 

 Why join us?  

At Bombardier, we design, build and maintain the world’s peak-performing aircraft for the world’s most discerning people and businesses, governments and militaries. We have been successful in setting the highest standards by putting our people at the heart of it all, and defining excellence, together.

Working at Bombardier means operating at the highest level. Every day, you are part of a team that delivers superior experiences and products, pushing the boundaries of what's possible in our industry and beyond. By prioritizing employee growth and development, we empower everyone to reach their full potential on their own terms, because the best work happens when you are free to be yourself and share your unique expertise. 

 Bombardier’s Benefits Program 

With our employees’ well-being top of mind, we offer a comprehensive and competitive Benefits Program, which includes the following: 

 • Insurance plans (Dental, medical, life insurance, disability, and more) 

 • Competitive base salary 

 • Retirement savings plan 

 • Employee Assistance Program  

 • Tele Health Program

 What are your contributions to the team? 

• Work in collaboration with the production department, the aircraft methods support group and the engineering department in our manufacturing facilities to analyze tool requests in order to find innovative technological solutions that will improve the business performances,

• Create, validate, issue estimates and cost analyses for all types of jigs used in the manufacturing and assembly of aircraft components,

• Participate, along with the tool designers, in the definition of the tool concepts,

• Issue order instructions to allow our external suppliers to manufacture tools as per our requirements and specific needs,

• Support our external suppliers during manufacturing,

• Ensure rigorous follow-up of each request to minimize delay,

• Inspect tools to ensure their conformity to drawings before delivery to production,

• Participate and support the aircraft methods support group and production during the first trial of the jigs,

• Provide technical support to the various production sectors,

• Assist operations during technical issues.

• Travel to different sites around the world, in order to carry out inspections and evaluations of various jigs.

 How to thrive in this role? 

• You have a college diploma in mechanical manufacturing or in aeronautics,

• You have 5 years of experience in a manufacturing environment,

• You know Catia V5 drawing software (asset),

• You have experience in project management,

• You have technical knowledge in mechanical manufacturing,

• You can work in French and English,

• You have good manual experience in the field of specialized tools,

• You know the aeronautical field and more precisely the interior finishing assembly,

• You have an analytical mind and a good sense of organization,

• You have excellent communication skills and enjoy teamwork,

• You know the Microsoft office suite.

 Now that you can see yourself in this role, apply and join the Bombardier Team! 

 Please note: You don’t need all the skills, knowledge, and experience listed to apply for this position. We’re not looking for the perfect candidate, we’re looking for great talent and passionate individuals. 

Bombardier is an equal opportunity employer and encourages persons of any race, religion, ethnicity, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, immigration status, disability or other applicable legally protected characteristics to apply.

jobs.desc:
At John Deere, we run so life can leap forward. This powerful purpose is our promise to humankind that we will dream, design, and deliver breakthrough products that sustain our world for generations to come. The world is counting on us to feed billions of people and build vital infrastructures in villages, towns and megacities. And we live up to the legacy our founder forged in a one-room blacksmith's shop nearly two centuries ago by creating a culture that brings out the best in all of us. A culture where great ideas thrive because every voice is heard.

 Primary Location:  United States (US) - Iowa  - Dubuque   

 As a   Machine Hand / Tool Room Machinist   with John Deere in Dubuque, IA, you will:  

 Set up and operate one or more machines such as lathes, mills, horizontal boring machine, etc., and perform machining operations consisting of many details on a wide variety of non-repetitive parts, holding close tolerances.  Work will be performed in a production environment focused on safety, quality, and teamwork.  

 Job details are dependent on duties assigned but in general consist of the following:  

• Work from drawings, sketches, prints, 3D models, samples, written or verbal instructions.  

• Perform own setups, work from part prints and job specifications.  

• Plan sequence of work to be performed and determine tools and equipment needed to carry work to completion.  

• Make all required mathematical calculations, lay out parts using measuring instruments and handbook tables.  

• Determine machine feed and speed for work involved.  

• Check own work for conformance to print and specifications.  

• Use various types of tools and equipment including material handling equipment, lathes, mills, horizontal boring machines, jigs, fixtures, measuring gages and instruments, and applicable hand and power tools.  

• Assist and support other team members and work with minimal supervision.  

• Clean work area and perform other miscellaneous duties inherent to the job.  

• Work shifts (choice of shift based on seniority).  

 Minimum Qualifications:    

• Must be at least 18 years of age.  

• Must have  at least one  of the following:  

• High School Diploma or G.E.D.  

• National Career Readiness Certificate (NCRC)  

• At least  3 years  of manufacturing work experience  

• Journeyperson’s card in Tool Room Machining  or  equivalent education / work experience (including applicable Military experience and training).  

• Includes at least 1 year of CNC machining experience 

• Includes at least 2 years of experience with tool room machining 

• Experience laying out and fabricating parts.  

• Experience utilizing precision measuring equipment and experience working from product design prints and sketches.  

• Ability to perform manual tasks related to described job duties for duration of work shift; including but not limited to frequent standing, walking, bending, and lifting.  

• Ability and willingness to work potential overtime (including weekends).  

 Why Work at John Deere? Why Work anywhere else?    

 If you strive to do great work, excel in creative environments, thrive in teams, and live for problem solving – this is the place for you.    

 At John Deere, your ideas, experiences, and values matter.   

 Please see below for a summary of the value of your John Deere career and total rewards available to you to support you and your well-being.    

• Highly competitive base pay and performance bonuses   

• Savings & Retirement benefits   

• Wellbeing – Physical and Mental Healthcare   

• Paid Holidays & Competitive Vacation Packages   

• Employee Assistance Programs   

• Tuition Assistance   

• Fitness subsidies and on-site gyms at specific Deere locations   

• Charitable contribution match   

• Rebate Program & numerous discount programs for personal use   

 John Deere is an equal opportunity employer.  All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.

jobs.title: Senior Mechanical Design & Analysis Engineer, Tooling
jobs.desc:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known. 

 Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us. 

 About the Team: 

 The Tooling and Factory Automation team sits at the intersection of design, manufacturing, and automation, making everything from large-scale structural fixtures to small tools that directly enable Terran R’s production. As a design group embedded within the manufacturing organization, we dig deep into the needs of our internal partners to understand root problems, propose solutions, and deliver hardware to help build faster, scale smarter, and work better. The team is also at the forefront of Relativity’s growing factory automation efforts, an increasingly critical part of scaling production of Terran R at existing and future facilities. You’ll have the autonomy to make decisions, field solutions, and see them in action on the factory floor. Ultimately, you’re not just designing tools or automated processes; you’re defining how rockets and factories get built. 

 About the Role: 

 The Mechanical Design Engineers are responsible for the design and development of tools and factory automation equipment that support manufacturing. The Mechanical Engineering team works closely with Design and Manufacturing, turning top-level requirements and concepts into functional delivered equipment. The Mechanical Design Engineering team brings a high level of innovation and ingenuity into the design process, as they are tasked with building out a highly automated production facility. 

• Develop high quality development and production tooling and automation solutions for the Terran vehicle and Aeon engine programs

• Capable of integrating concepts and principles of mechanical design and analysis of several different projects in a fast-paced environment - projects will vary in size and scale 

• Ability to interpret and apply sound design and drafting standards (ASME Y14.5) in creating tooling drawing definitions 

• Handle a wide range of technical problems and familiar with all types of material handling, assembly fixtures, off-loaders, rotisseries, test fixtures, structural weldments, environmental chambers, and custom machines 

• Close collaboration with component designers, manufacturing engineers, and integration engineering to achieve the best possible cradle to grave metrics (safety, cost, quality, cycle time, delivery, reliability, life, and maintenance/refurbishment) 

• Manage projects including vendor selection, fabrication, inspection, equipment installation, and commissioning of tooling 

 About You: 

• Bachelor of Science degree in manufacturing engineering, mechanical engineering or equivalent 

• 6+ years of work or project experience with design, build, and commissioning of tooling and fixtures for manufacturing, assembly and test 

• Experience using CAD and FEA-based analysis software (NX and ANSYS Workbench preferred) for structural applications 

• Experience in full-cycle project completion 

• Experience in strategic buildout and project management of tooling supporting production 

 Nice to haves but not required: 

• Strong expertise in design for manufacturability and design for assembly including experience taking products from prototype design to production 

• Solid understanding of common manufacturing materials, GD&T, and tolerance/stack-up analysis 

• Solid understanding of common manufacturing processes and machines including mills, lathes, welding, sheet-metal bending, lifting/rigging, assembly, inspection, etc. 

• Experience with custom machine design: motors, actuators, linear rails/actuators, pneumatics, bearings, etc.

 Compensation is only one part of our total rewards package. Relativity Space offers competitive salary and equity, a generous PTO and sick leave policy, parental leave, an annual learning and development stipend, and more! To see some of the benefits & perks we offer, please visit here.

jobs.title: Project Manager, Tooling (Starship)
jobs.desc:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

 PROJECT MANAGER, TOOLING (STARSHIP) 

 You own contractor execution, schedule, and contracted-labor cost to install, activate, and commission Gigabay / Starfactory tooling and infrastructure. Engineering owns design and hardware procurement. This IC role is based at Starbase, Texas.

 RESPONSIBILITIES: 

• Own field execution, contracted-labor cost, and schedule for tooling and infrastructure projects (steel structures, lifting/access equipment, production stations, and related mechanical systems)

• Issue and manage POs for contract labor; manage shipments, on-site assembly, erection, install, activation, and commissioning

• Own a rolling 2-week look-ahead and provide daily updates on accomplishments, progress, and blockers

• Own and coordinate inputs to the overall Gigabay schedule; align installs with facility-level critical path

• Write and manage construction contracts; track and approve invoicing for contracted labor

• Supervise technicians and contractors in the field (no direct reports)

• Lead mechanical and structural execution; coordinate contractors and internal teams for power, fluids, and electrical as required to deliver a complete, activated system

• After engineering completes first-article station builds, own subsequent station installs through activation, including internal and external labor

• Work daily with responsible engineers on constructibility, status, and technical escalations; coordinate other construction teams at interfaces

• Use CAD (NX preferred) to sequence installs, check clearances, and verify field conditions against the model

• Issue work packages / manufacturing plans for internal welding and toolmaking so internal and contractor work stay sequenced

• Perform daily quality inspection of contractor work; stop work and escalate when field conditions do not match design or site safety requirements

• Plan installs around live Gigabay operations so production and construction do not block each other

 BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: 

• 2+ years managing external contractors on industrial or construction installs, including issuing POs or contracts and driving work through install, activation, and closeout

• Ability to navigate CAD models (e.g. NX, SolidWorks, CATIA, or similar)

• High school diploma or equivalency certificate

 PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: 

• Bachelor’s degree in construction management, engineering, architecture, or a related field

• Experience with heavy lifts, rigging, access systems, crane/jib installs, or similar industrial equipment

• Experience coordinating power, fluids, and electrical tie-ins to complete a mechanical/structural install

• Experience owning repeatable production-station or tooling installs after a first-article process

• Ability to navigate large NX assemblies and drawings

• Experience directing technicians and contractors without formal direct reports

• Strong daily communication with engineering, technicians, contractors, and leadership

 ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: 

• Occasional travel to other SpaceX sites with similar projects

• Work schedule may vary based on site operational needs. Must be willing to support planned shift changes, extended hours, and weekends when required to meet critical path

• Physical effort including standing, lifting, climbing, bending, grasping, sitting, pulling, pushing, stooping, stretching, and carrying as generally required to perform the functions of this position

• Work performed in an active industrial / construction environment

• Valid driver’s license

• Stand: Up to 6 hours per day

• Sit: Up to 3 hours per day

• Push/Pull: Up to 75lbs. (unassisted) 2 hours or longer per day

• Overhead reach: Up to 1 hour per day

• Walk: Up to 3 hours per day

• Lift/Carry: Up to 50lbs. (unassisted) 2 hours or longer per day

• Climb (ladder/stairs): Up to 3 hours per day

• Kneel/Crouch: Up to 3 hours per day

• Upper body twist: Up to 3 hours per day

• Ability to work in temperatures over 80 degrees up to 3 hours per day

• Candidate must be capable of safely using an air purifying respirator, operating heavy equipment and machinery, and performing the physical requirements of the job listed in the job description. jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer
jobs.desc:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE TEAM

 Anduril’s Manufacturing Engineering team is responsible for rapidly iterating, scaling, and sustaining cutting-edge defense hardware, including static sensor towers, autonomous ground systems, and high-performance flight vehicles. We bridge the gap between design engineering and physical hardware execution. 

 As a Manufacturing Engineer on 1st Shift (6:00 am to 3:00 pm), you will serve as the primary mechanical and assembly authority on the factory floor. You will have a dual mandate: partner deeply with R&D during early architecture to drive rigorous Design for Assembly and Manufacturing (DFA/DFM), and architect the physical assembly processes, precision tooling, and integration lines required to scale complex mechanical hardware from prototype to high-rate production. 

 This is a heavily mechanical, hands-on role. You will design assembly fixtures in 3D CAD, perform tolerance stack-up analyses, define structural joining and bonding procedures, integrate smart-tooling systems, and establish repeatable, error-proofed mechanical assembly lines. 

 WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Design for Assembly & Manufacturability (DFA/DFM): 

• Embed directly with Mechanical Design Engineering during early R&D phases to influence product architecture, driving aggressive part reduction, standard fastener consolidation, and modular sub-assembly design. 

• Conduct detailed 1D and 2D worst-case and statistical (RSS) tolerance stack-up analyses to ensure mechanical interfaces, datum structures, dynamic clearances, and pin/hole alignments assemble consistently without force-fitting. 

• Define hardware assembly strategies, joint clamping designs, thermal interface material (TIM) applications, structural bonding, and torque sequencing early in the CAD development cycle. 

• Tooling, Jigs, & Assembly Fixture Design: 

• Own end-to-end mechanical design of production tooling—including precision assembly jigs, alignment nests, press-fit tooling, ergonomic lift/handling equipment, and mechanical verification fixtures using 3D CAD (NX or SolidWorks). 

• Apply finite element analysis (FEA) where necessary to validate fixture rigidity, deflection under clamping loads, and stress concentrations. 

• Produce fully detailed 2D fabrication drawings utilizing ASME Y14.5 Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerancing (GD&T) for internal machine shops or external toolmakers. 

• Mechanical Assembly Process Engineering: 

• Line Architecture & Flow: Design, sequence, and balance complex, multi-stage mechanical assembly lines. Define takt times, line layouts, and ergonomic workstations to transition hardware seamlessly from sub-assembly to final structural integration. 

• Joining & Fastening Technologies: Establish and qualify robust fastening processes, including torque-tension specifications, torque-angle control, bolt pre-load engineering, and press-fit/interference-fit operations (bearings, bushings, dowels). 

• Adhesives, Sealing, & Dispensing: Develop repeatable application methods for chemical assembly processes, including structural bonding (epoxies, urethanes), thread locking, environmental gasketing/RTV sealing, potting, and Thermal Interface Material (TIM) dispensing. 

• Precision Mechanical Alignment & Calibration: Develop standard processes, measurement techniques, and alignment procedures for precision kinematic mechanisms, optical/sensor payloads, gimbals, and dynamic structural joints. 

• Error-Proofing & Quality Integration: Lead Process Failure Mode and Effects Analyses (pFMEAs) for mechanical assembly workflows. Design physical error-proofing (Poka-Yoke) mechanisms, go/no-go verification gauges, and smart-tool integration (DC electric torque tools with digital data logging) to eliminate assembly errors. 

• Work Definition & Operator Enablement: Author visual, step-by-step Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and digital work instructions that clearly define mechanical assembly sequences, critical tool callouts, fastener specs, and quality inspection gates. 

• NPI Ramp, Sustainment, & Root Cause Analysis: 

• Lead technical disposition and first-principles root-cause investigations (8D, 5-Whys, Fishbone) on mechanical assembly failures, binding mechanisms, structural interferences, and joint integrity issues. 

• Bridge the gap between engineering intent and production execution by converting Engineering Bills of Materials (eBOMs) into logical, modular Manufacturing Bills of Materials (mBOMs) within PLM (Teamcenter). 

• Author and implement Engineering Change Orders (ECOs/ECRs) for mechanical modifications, hardware deviations, and assembly drawing updates. 

 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• B.S. in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or a closely related technical field. 

• 3+ years of experience in manufacturing or mechanical design role with heavy exposure to mechanical assembly and hardware integration (aerospace, defense, automotive, dynamic robotics, or precision industrial hardware). 

• Proficiency in 3D CAD modeling (Siemens NX strongly preferred; SolidWorks, CATIA, or Creo acceptable) with a strong portfolio of designed and deployed assembly tooling, nests, or fixtures. 

• Advanced working knowledge of ASME Y14.5 GD&T—ability to design assembly

jobs.title: Sr. Tooling Designer, Investment Casting
jobs.desc:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

 SR. TOOLING DESIGNER, INVESTMENT CASTING 

 SpaceX is seeking a Sr. Tooling Designer for Investment Casting, to own the design and development of wax injection molds and ceramic core injection molds used to produce turbine blades and vanes. This role is critical to scaling reliable, high-performance cast components. You will design complex tooling that must repeatedly deliver extremely tight tolerances and intricate internal cooling geometries while supporting aggressive rate and cost targets. 

 As a member of the materials team, you will work closely with materials, casting, and manufacturing engineers to develop tooling solutions from concept through production qualification. Your designs will directly impact casting yield, dimensional stability, and the overall manufacturability of mission-critical hardware. 

 RESPONSIBILITIES : 

• Design high-precision wax injection molds and ceramic core injection molds for complex turbine blades and vanes to be manufactured in-house 

• Interpret and enable mold filling simulations and apply first-principles analysis to optimize gating, venting, cooling, and shrinkage compensation 

• Account for multi-stage shrinkage (wax, ceramic, and alloy) to consistently meet stringent dimensional and metallurgical requirements 

• Own tooling designs from concept through tryout, qualification, and production release 

• Own and manage the feasibility and surfacing of critical mold components 

• Collaborate closely casting engineers, materials scientists, and vendors to troubleshoot tooling-related casting defects and improve yield 

• Apply advanced GD&T and tolerance stack-up analysis to complex airfoil geometries 

• Support design for manufacturability (DFM) initiatives to enable high-rate production while maintaining quality and cost targets 

• Interface with internal manufacturing teams and external tooling vendors to ensure designs are successfully translated into reliable production tooling 

• Drive continuous improvement of tooling standards, materials, and maintenance practices for high-volume casting operations 

 BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: 

• 5+ years of professional experience designing high-precision injection molds for wax patterns AND ceramics 

• 3+ years of feasibility for wax patterns AND ceramics 

• Experience with Siemens NX 

 PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: 

• In-depth knowledge of wax and ceramic material behavior, rheology, and processing 

• Extensive knowledge of wax and ceramic tool design requirements 

• Knowledge of drafting practices and principles 

• Direct experience designing molds used in the production of turbine blades and vanes 

• Demonstrated success taking complex tooling from design through production qualification 

• Deep understanding of the investment casting process and associated shrinkage/ distortion mechanisms 

• Experience working in a fast-paced, high-mix manufacturing environment 

• Hands-on experience supporting mold tryouts and casting process development 

• Experience with manufacturing wax pattern and ceramic tooling, including CNC and mold making 

 ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: 

• Willingness to work extended hours and weekends when required to support hardware delivery and production campaigns 

• Must be willing to travel (up to 25%) to external suppliers and other SpaceX facilities 

 ITAR REQUIREMENTS: 

• To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here . 

 SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

jobs.title: Methods Engineer
jobs.desc:
At Alstom, we understand transport networks and what moves people. From high-speed trains, metros, monorails, and trams, to turnkey systems, services, infrastructure, signalling and digital mobility, we offer our diverse customers the broadest portfolio in the industry. Every day, 80,000 colleagues lead the way to greener and smarter mobility worldwide, connecting cities as we reduce carbon and replace cars. 

 Could you be the full-time onsite Methods Engineer* in West Mifflin, PA (Pittsburgh area) we’re looking for? 

 * Candidates who are recent graduates with internship experience are also encouraged to apply. 

 Your future role 

 Take on a new challenge and apply your manufacturing and process engineering expertise in a new cutting-edge field. You'll play a crucial role in defining and validating detailed manufacturing processes for new products, creating industrial documentation, and driving continuous improvement initiatives to enhance efficiency and quality. Day-to-day, you’ll work closely with teams across the business (such as Process Engineers, Product Design teams, and Quality Assurance), lead the industrialization of retrofit processes following engineering changes, and ensure optimal EHS and ergonomic conditions—and much more. 

 We’ll look to you for: 

• Contributing ideas to the Process Engineer or PIM to enhance product manufacturability and meet QCD (Quality, Cost, Delivery) targets, 

• Participating in product design reviews as necessary, 

• Collaborating on Process Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (P-FMEA) and validating prototypes, 

• Requesting tooling as needed and writing detailed tooling specifications, 

• Ensuring optimal EHS (Environment, Health, and Safety) and ergonomic conditions, 

• Performing task sequencing for workstations and calculating accurate method times, 

• Industrializing retrofit processes following engineering changes to include routings, work instructions, and tooling, 

• Leading continuous process improvement initiatives, 

• Acting as a champion for Alstom Performance System (APSYS), 

• Developing and managing ERP routings and work/inspection instructions. 

 All about you 

 We value passion and attitude over experience. That’s why we don’t expect you to have every single skill. Instead, we’ve listed some that we think will help you succeed and grow in this role: 

• 
 Bachelor’s degree in Industrial, Process, Manufacturing, Mechanical, or Electrical Engineering , 

• 
 Candidates may include new graduates with internships or up to ~5 years of hands‑on experience. 

• Experience or understanding of manufacturing processes and methods , 

• Preferred experience in a manufacturing or assembly environment (electrical/mechanical assembly work is especially relevant). 

• Demonstrated ability or exposure to process documentation and improvement, 

• Familiarity with Quality, EHS standards, and Ergonomics, 

• Strong communication skills in English (verbal and written), 

• Technical knowledge of Manufacturing Engineering, including writing manufacturing work instructions and line balancing, 

• Familiarity with Process FMEA and QRQC (Quick Response Quality Control), 

• Experience with time analysis methodologies (e.g., MTM, MEK, UAS), 

• Ability to contribute to continuous improvement initiatives, 

• Willingness and ability to travel up to 10% for work. 

 Things you’ll enjoy 

 Join us on a life-long transformative journey – the rail industry is here to stay, so you can grow and develop new skills and experiences throughout your career. You’ll also: 

• Collaborate with transverse teams and helpful colleagues, 

• Work with cutting-edge manufacturing processes and advanced industrial tools to shape innovative solutions, 

• Progress towards becoming a key contributor in driving operational excellence and continuous improvement initiatives, 

• Utilise our dynamic and inclusive working environment, fostering collaboration, resilience, and a mindset of continuous learning, 

• Contribute to innovative projects, 

• Steer your career in whatever direction you choose across functions and countries, 

• Benefit from our investment in your development, through award-winning learning, 

• Benefit from a fair and dynamic reward package that recognises your performance and potential, plus comprehensive and competitive social coverage (life, medical, 401k). 

 You don’t need to be a train enthusiast to thrive with us. We guarantee that when you step onto one of our trains with your friends or family, you’ll be proud. If you’re up for the challenge, we’d love to hear from you! 

 Important to note 

 As a global business, we’re an equal-opportunity employer that celebrates diversity across the 63 countries we operate in. We’re committed to creating an inclusive workplace for everyone.

By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE TEAM 

The Maneuver Dominance team is building Thunder - an autonomous attack rotorcraft built to fight alongside crewed combat aviation to deliver overwhelming mass effects deep beyond the front lines. The team in London builds the Mission System and the autonomy that makes aircraft like Thunder work.

Autonomy is only as good as the link that carries it. Thunder is a compact airframe with weapons, sensors and radios competing for the same antenna real estate, flying low and in formation, in a spectrum that is actively contested. That is the problem you would own. 

ABOUT THE JOB 

Anduril is seeking a Senior Mechanical Engineer, Test Fixture Design to join the Thunder team in our Costa Mesa, CA office. Flight test validation moves only as fast as your ground test infrastructure allows. In this role, you will own the physical architecture, mechanical design, and rapid build of mission-critical test fixtures, structural test frames, and surrogate vehicle systems. Your hardware will validate everything from high-density avionics integration and dynamic payload releases to rotor vibration survivability and full-vehicle "iron bird" ground setups.

You will bridge the digital design and physical test worlds. Acting with high ownership and autonomy, you will derive load cases, architect rigid and reconfigurable test stands, integrate test instrumentation (sensors, load cells, actuators), and collaborate closely with machine shops and assembly technicians to bring test beds to life in days and weeks—not months.

• Lead the end-to-end mechanical design, analysis, and build of structural test fixtures, environmental/vibration test adapters, surrogate aircraft frames, and subsystem validation rigs.

• Take hands-on ownership of prototyping test equipment, operating machine tools, coordinating with internal model shops, and assembling complex ground test setups.

• Engineer rugged, rigid, and safe fixtures capable of reacting severe static and dynamic flight loads while maintaining precise interface tolerances and metrology alignment.

• Collaborate with Test, Electrical, and Systems teams to package actuators, load cells, LVDTs, strain gauges, and fluid/power lines seamlessly into test rigs.

• Partner with machine shops, material suppliers, and outside vendors; aggressively chase down lead times, resolve manufacturing anomalies, and optimize designs for DFM.

• Perform rapid stress, deflection, and fatigue calculations to verify that test fixtures possess adequate structural margins and will not influence test article dynamics.

• Travel to test ranges, environmental labs, and flight line facilities to deploy, troubleshoot, and support ground testing and critical customer demonstrations.

• BS or MS in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.

• 7+ years of professional mechanical engineering experience, with significant focus on mechanical design, structural tooling, test fixtures, or dynamic test equipment.

• High proficiency in 3D CAD modeling (Siemens NX preferred) and detailed engineering drawing creation adhering to ASME Y14.5 GD&T standards.

• Strong first-principles foundation in structural mechanics, load paths, structural steel/aluminum design, weldments, and bolt joint analysis.

• Proven hands-on prototyping and shop fabrication skills (manual/CNC machining, sheet metal, welding, 3D printing, hand tools).

• Demonstrated ability to move rapidly from concept to physical hardware in low-cycle, fast-turnaround prototyping environments.

• Willingness to travel ~25% to support off-site integration, testing, and hardware demonstrations.

• Must be eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

• Direct experience designing aerospace qualification fixtures (shaker table fixtures, drop test frames, centrifuge fixtures, or static load test frames).

• Deep proficiency in Siemens NX and Teamcenter.

• Experience integrating test instrumentation, sensors, hydraulic/pneumatic actuators, or Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) test setups.

• Working knowledge of MIL-STD-810, DO-160, or aerospace structural qualification testing procedures.

• Familiarity with finite element analysis (FEA) for structural stiffness and modal/vibration response analysis.

• Experience with collegiate build teams (e.g., Formula SAE, Baja SAE, Design Build Fly).

jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer II, Autonomous Airpower
jobs.desc:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE TEAM 

 The Air Dominance and Strike Division is one of Anduril’s fastest growing, most technically complex divisions. We develop and build collaborative combat aircraft, missiles, and the software that powers these autonomous weapons. We are scaling production of autonomous aircraft across our manufacturing facilities. Manufacturing Engineering drives process development, production readiness, and the transition from prototype to rate — ensuring that what Design engineers create can be built reliably, repeatedly, and at scale.

 ABOUT THE JOB 

 Anduril is seeking a Manufacturing Engineer II to join the Autonomous Airpower manufacturing team in Costa Mesa, California. You will own portions of the manufacturing value chain for autonomous aircraft hardware — implementing and refining manufacturing processes to hit production targets and quality standards. This role spans the full breadth of manufacturing engineering disciplines and may focus on one or more of the following areas depending on your background: structures and composites, mechanical systems (landing gear, doors, actuators), fluid systems (hydraulic, fuel, pneumatic), propulsion integration, avionics, or harnessing and electrical integration.

 At this level, you are expected to execute manufacturing engineering projects with moderate supervision, manage your own timelines and priorities, and begin mentoring junior engineers and technicians. You bring solid manufacturing fundamentals, hands-on experience on a production floor, and the ability to analyze workflows, identify bottlenecks, and drive targeted improvements. You are comfortable designing tooling and fixtures, troubleshooting production issues in real time, and translating technical constraints into actionable information for cross-functional partners.

 WHAT YOU’LL DO 

• Own the manufacturing value chain for assigned aircraft subsystems or assemblies — from process development through work instruction authoring, tooling definition, and production support

• Implement and refine manufacturing processes to achieve production targets and quality standards for your subsystems

• Analyze current workflows to identify bottlenecks and drive targeted cycle time reductions

• Author and maintain work instructions, quality plans, inspection requirements, and manufacturing BOMs that enable technicians to build hardware consistently

• Proficiently utilize CAD software to design tooling, fixtures, and production layouts for aircraft assemblies

• Provide DFM/DFA feedback to design engineering, communicating manufacturing constraints and suggesting alternatives based on hands-on production experience

• Execute assigned manufacturing engineering projects — managing timelines, coordinating with vendors and internal teams, and tracking progress to engineering leadership

• Troubleshoot production issues in real time, developing practical solutions to minimize downtime on the factory floor

• Apply Lean and Six Sigma tools (5S, value stream mapping, FMEA) to specific production areas and lead smaller improvement initiatives

• Mentor junior engineers and technicians, providing guidance on routine assignments and manufacturing best practices

 WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR 

• 4+ years of manufacturing engineering experience in aerospace, defense, or complex hardware production environments

• Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Aerospace, Manufacturing, Electrical, or Industrial Engineering or equivalent hands-on manufacturing experience

• Demonstrated experience implementing and refining manufacturing processes on a production floor

• Experience authoring work instructions, manufacturing plans, and quality documentation for hardware builds

• Proficiency with CAD tools (CATIA, SolidWorks, NX, or equivalent) for tooling and fixture design

• Experience managing manufacturing engineering projects including timelines, vendor coordination, and resource allocation

• Hands-on troubleshooting experience in a production environment

• Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 

• Experience in one or more of the following: composite structures, mechanical systems (landing gear, flight controls, doors), fluid systems (hydraulic, fuel, pneumatic), propulsion, avionics integration, or wire harness manufacturing

• Experience transitioning hardware from prototype or first-article builds to rate production

• Experience with aircraft or autonomous vehicle assembly

• Knowledge of AS9100, aerospace quality systems, and non-conformance management processes

• Experience applying Lean, Six Sigma, or structured continuous improvement methodologies

• Experience working with Teamcenter, SAP, Oracle, or similar PLM/ERP platforms

• Active U.S. Secret security clearance

jobs.title: Signalling Hardware Design Engineer
jobs.desc:
Req ID:496484  

 ​ 

 At Alstom, we understand transport networks and what moves people. From high-speed trains, metros, monorails, and trams, to turnkey systems, services, infrastructure, signalling and digital mobility, we offer our diverse customers the broadest portfolio in the industry. Every day, more than 80 000 colleagues lead the way to greener and smarter mobility worldwide, connecting cities as we reduce carbon and replace cars. 

 Could you be the full-time Interlocking (IXL) Hardware Design Engineer in Toronto, ON, we’re looking for?

 Your future role 

 Take on a new challenge and apply your technical expertise in a cutting-edge field. You’ll work alongside collaborative and innovative teammates.

 You'll play a pivotal role in ensuring the safe and efficient movement of trains by designing and standardizing Interlocking (IXL) system architectures and configurations. Day-to-day, you’ll work closely with teams across the business (Project IXL Design Leaders, V&V teams, Installation & Testing teams), analyze customer and product requirements, and contribute to continuous improvement in hardware solutions.

 You’ll specifically take care of designing hardware configurations, power distribution architectures, and documentation for signaling equipment, but also support project deployment and debugging activities.

 We’ll look to you for:

• 
 Delivering design scheme plan layouts, hardware configuration drawings, BOPs, BOMs, and signaling equipment room layouts.

• 
 Designing AC/DC power distribution architectures, including main distribution panels and subpanels for redundant signaling systems.

• 
 Performing power load analysis and designing backup power configurations using battery backups, UPS, and automatic transfer switches.

• 
 Ensuring adherence to reference application design methods and tools, requesting deviations when necessary.

• 
 Participating actively in IXL detailed design review meetings and providing activity progress reports.

• 
 Organizing and producing hardware design deliverables in accordance with project templates and requirements.

• 
 Supporting project teams in debugging design issues and analyzing design change requests.

• 
 Defining pre-fitted solutions for IXL equipment, including racks, cubicles, and cabling, while ensuring proper testing and documentation.

• 
 Collaborating with multidisciplinary teams to capture hardware interfaces, environmental conditions, and application constraints.

• 
 Sharing knowledge of IXL system architecture features with the engineering community.

 All about you 

 We value passion and attitude over experience. That’s why we don’t expect you to have every single skill. Instead, we’ve listed some that we think will help you succeed and grow in this role:

• 
 Engineering Bachelor’s degree in Electrical, Electronic, Automation Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

• 
 P. Eng certification or in progress

• 
 5-10 years of experience in systems/sub-systems application design, integration, or electrotechnical product development in a complex and regulated environment (e.g., railway signaling, aerospace, defense).

• 
 Good analytical skills and prior experience in system design & integration.

• 
 Knowledge of Interlocking Systems, safety principles, and power supply design.

• 
 Familiarity with Alstom products (desirable).

• 
 Strong problem-solving, writing, and communication skills, with an open-minded and multidisciplinary approach.

• 
 Fluency in English.

 Things you’ll enjoy Join us on a life-long transformative journey – the rail industry is here to stay, so you can grow and develop new skills and experiences throughout your career. You’ll also:

• 
 Enjoy stability, challenges, and a long-term career free from boring daily routines.

• 
 Work with new security standards for rail signaling.

• 
 Collaborate with transverse teams and helpful colleagues.

• 
 Contribute to innovative projects.

• 
 Utilize our flexible and inclusive working environment.

• 
 Steer your career in whatever direction you choose across functions and countries.

• 
 Benefit from our investment in your development through award-winning learning programs.

• 
 Progress towards leadership roles or specialized technical expertise.

• 
 Benefit from a fair and dynamic reward package that recognizes your performance and potential, plus comprehensive and competitive social coverage (life, medical, pension).

 Compensation 

 The expected compensation for this role is $100,000 – $135,000 CAD per year, plus benefits and eligibility for an annual performance bonus. Final compensation will be based on skills, experience, and internal equity.

 Use of Artificial Intelligence in Hiring 

 We do not use artificial intelligence in the recruiting process for this role.

 Interview Process & Candidate Communication 

 Candidates who participate in an interview for this role will be informed of the hiring decision within 45 days of their final interview date.

 This job posting represents an existing vacancy

 You don’t need to be a train enthusiast to thrive with us. We guarantee that when you step onto one of our trains with your friends or family, you’ll be proud. If you’re up for the challenge, we’d love to hear from you! 

 Important to note 

As a global business, we’re an equal-opportunity employer that celebrates diversity across the 63 countries we operate in. We’re committed to creating an inclusive workplace for everyone.
