jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer II, Barracuda
jobs.desc:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE SITE 

 Anduril, a leader in autonomous systems and weapons manufacturing, is building Arsenal-1, its first hyper-scale manufacturing facility, just south of Columbus, Ohio in Pickaway County. Arsenal-1 is redefining the scale and speed at which autonomous systems and weapons can be produced for the United States and its allies and partners. This is a monumental and essential step toward rebuilding America's defense industrial base, strengthening America's warfighting capabilities, and enhancing deterrence amid rising international threats.

 ABOUT THE PRODUCT 

 The future of defense is being built right now, and Anduril's Barracuda product is at its leading edge. Barracuda is a family of air-breathing autonomous air vehicles (AAVs) purpose-built for hyper-scale production and mass employment. The Barracuda family consists of Barracuda-100, Barracuda-250, and Barracuda-500. Each increment offers increasing size, range, and payload capacity, but all Barracudas are compatible with a host of payloads and employment mechanisms, support a variety of different missions, and provide warfighters with an adaptable and upgradeable capability to counter evolving threats.

 ABOUT THE TEAM 

 The Barracuda Launch Team (BLT) will set the standard for building the future at Arsenal-1, our state-of-the-art manufacturing facility in Ashville, OH. As Barracuda transitions from low-rate initial production at Anduril HQ to high-rate manufacturing at Arsenal-1, this team will own the technology transfer, stand up production lines, and sustain the floor operations that make that ramp possible. You will have the opportunity to train under our world-class manufacturing team at Anduril HQ in Costa Mesa, CA for up to 2 months before bringing that standard of excellence back to Ohio.

 ABOUT THE JOB 

 As a Manufacturing Engineer II, you will independently own manufacturing processes and sub-assemblies for Barracuda as production transfers from Anduril HQ and scales to high rate at Arsenal-1. You'll manage the full lifecycle of your area's build package — work instructions, MBOMs, process specs, and MES configuration — while driving line optimization and yield improvement on the floor. This role demands someone who can troubleshoot complex electromechanical integration issues in real time, own RCCA from identification through implementation, and translate production data into tangible process gains.

 ** This role requires relocation to Costa Mesa, CA for an initial training program of up to 2 months. Housing, transportation, etc. will be provided during your stay. 

 WHAT YOU'LL DO 

• Execute the manufacturing of Barracuda products and sub-assemblies involving complex electromechanical integration from prototype through full-rate production, and own the complete build package for your area.

• Author and maintain all production documentation — work instructions, MBOMs, tooling and fixture specs, process specifications — ensuring they stay current as designs evolve and production scales.

• Drive line optimization in your area: analyze takt times, cycle times, and throughput data to identify bottlenecks and implement process changes that improve rate and efficiency.

• Root-cause and resolve floor issues using RCCA and 5-Why methodologies; own corrective actions through implementation and verify effectiveness via yield and quality data.

• Monitor and improve first-pass yield and defect rates; use statistical process control to identify variation and drive process stability.

• Manage MES transactions and configuration for your production area, ensuring accurate real-time traceability, work order management, and production reporting.

• Implement Lean and Six Sigma tools (5S, VSM, FMEA) in your production area; lead smaller kaizen events and standardize successful modifications across lines.

• Support technology transfer of Barracuda production processes from HQ to Arsenal-1, validating processes, tooling, and quality standards in the new facility.

• Diagnose complex equipment and tooling issues, configure and optimize parameters, and collaborate with vendors to resolve technical problems.

• Participate in design reviews to provide DFM input; collaborate with quality engineers to develop process control parameters that ensure product specifications.

• Mentor junior engineers and technicians, building team capability in electromechanical assembly processes and manufacturing best practices.

jobs.title: Senior Manufacturing Engineer
jobs.desc:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB 

 Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

 ABOUT THE ROLE 

 Manufacturing Engineering powers Rocket Lab’s factories from concept to full-scale production. We turn early ideas into manufacturable designs, build and optimise the systems that make them real, and constantly push for faster, better, smarter ways to build. We engineer the factories that build the rockets, boosting quality, cutting cost, and accelerating build rate.  

 We're seeking experienced Senior Manufacturing Engineers across multiple disciplines to take ownership of complex products, lead problem-solving initiatives, and drive manufacturing excellence. 

 THE OPPORTUNITIES: 

 We're hiring across four key manufacturing disciplines: 

• Assembly & Integration  – Mechanical, Assembly, Propulsion, Mechanical Test 

• Avionics & Test  – Electronics manufacturing, electrical test, debugging systems 

• Composites  – Advanced materials, resins, ablatives, sandwich structures 

• Machining  – CNC programming, precision manufacturing, GD&T 

 In your application, please indicate which discipline(s) align with your experience and interests. 

 YOU’LL GET TO: 

• Own & Ship: 

• Own products in production as the go-to expert 

• Drive teams to hit production targets at top quality 

• Execute product improvements and design qualifications 

• Solve & Fix: 

• Lead root cause analysis and corrective actions on failures 

• Disposition non-conformances on flight hardware using engineering judgment and risk assessment 

• Bridge production, quality, supply chain, and design engineering for rapid problem-solving 

• Build & Improve: 

• Create bulletproof production procedures and processes 

• Design reliable assemblies and test fixtures 

• Develop mission-critical test methods for safety-critical systems 

• Champion Lean/Six Sigma continuous improvement 

• Lead & Scale: 

• Drive design reviews as DFM/DFT expert 

• Launch new products and revisions into production 

• Plan and execute capital equipment upgrades with business cases 

• Implement planning, quality, ERP, and data systems 

• Mentor & Deliver: 

• Train engineers and production teams 

• Break down complex projects and deliver on time 

• Establish and execute project plans autonomously 

• Maintain product manuals and lessons-learned docs 

 WHAT YOU BRING: 

 The Must-Haves: 

• Engineering degree (Electrical, Mechanical, Mechatronics, Chemical, Materials, or related) 

• 5+ years manufacturing/production/process engineering in the trenches 

• Well-tested debugging complex systems on the factory floor 

• You ship results independently and lead teams to do the same 

• You influence stakeholders, assess risk fast, and implement lasting solutions 

• Thrive in high pressure environments – can hustle and built for speed 

 Your Specialty (one or more): 

• Avionics & Test: Expert-level debugging of electro-mechanical systems, instrumentation (oscilloscopes, power supplies, sensors, serial devices) 

• Composites: Deep knowledge of resins, ablatives, sandwich structures, tooling, and manufacturing processes 

• Machining: Advanced GD&T, inspection methods, CAM software (3/5-axis CNC), 3+ years shop experience 

• Assembly & Integration: Led mechanical assembly, integration, propulsion, or mechanical test operations 

 Extra Edge: 

• Aerospace/defence/high-reliability manufacturing background 

• Lean/Six Sigma certified 

• ERP/PLM systems (Siemens TeamCenter, Infor LN) 

• DFMEA, PFMEA, Fault Tree, root cause/corrective action expert 

• SPC, capacity modelling, value stream mapping 

• Environmental testing (vibe, shock, thermal, vacuum) 

• Mentored or led engineers 

 WHAT WE EXPECT FROM YOU: 

 You own it. Problems become solutions. Documentation gets done. Projects ship on time. You communicate clearly, lead when needed, support teammates always, and show up ready to build the future. 

 We take delivery incredibly seriously. Failure is not in our DNA. The work is hard, demanding, and not for the faint-hearted. 

 You don't go to Mars working eight to five, Monday to Friday. If you're a high performer, hungry for work with genuine impact where your engineering excellence directly shapes space exploration, national security, and critical infrastructure, you've found your place. 

 In return, you'll solve problems that actually matter alongside experts who run toward challenges, not away from them. 

 If this resonates with you, apply today! 
 WHAT TO EXPECT 

 We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.

 FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN US OFFICES ONLY: 

 To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), Rocket Lab Employees must be a U.S. citizen, lawful U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State and/or the U.S. Department of Commerce, as applicable. jobs.title: Staff Technical Program Manager, Tooling & Automation
jobs.desc:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known. 

 Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us. 

 About the Team: 

 The Tooling and Factory Automation team sits at the intersection of design, manufacturing, and automation, making everything from large-scale structural fixtures to small tools that directly enable Terran R’s production. As a design group embedded within the manufacturing organization, we dig deep into the needs of our internal partners to understand root problems, propose solutions, and deliver hardware to help build faster, scale smarter, and work better. The team is also at the forefront of Relativity’s growing factory automation efforts, an increasingly critical part of scaling production of Terran R at existing and future facilities. You’ll have the autonomy to make decisions, field solutions, and see them in action on the factory floor. Ultimately, you’re not just delivering tools or automated processes; you’re defining how rockets and factories get built. 

 About the Role: 

• Collaborate with leadership to forge a strategic growth roadmap for the Tooling and Factory Automation org that propels company-wide objectives and partnerships 

• Create and facilitate team infrastructure in the form of frameworks, digital productivity tools, and physical resources 

• Coordinate people, scope, timelines, interactions and communications to achieve the highest standards of team effectiveness and service to customers 

• Contribute to innovation through direct engagement in design activities and definition of strategic technological initiatives 

• Establish and track metrics that define the team’s impact 

 About You: 

• Degree in engineering, science, mathematics, or related fields; mechanical, aerospace or electrical engineering degree preferred 

• 5+ years in program or project management role(s) 

• Experience managing multiple customers across matrix organizations and building sustainable processes 

• Experience in the manufacturing of complex parts and assemblies 

• Proven ability to solve challenging technical problems and develop robust, scalable solutions 

 Nice to haves but not required: 

• Experience in the development and integration of tooling and automated manufacturing equipment 

• High volume manufacturing experience 

 At Relativity Space, we are committed to transparency and fairness in our compensation practices. Actual compensation will be determined based on experience, qualifications, and other job-related factors. 

 Compensation is only one part of our total rewards package. Relativity Space offers competitive salary and equity, a generous PTO and sick leave policy, parental leave, an annual learning and development stipend, and more! To see some of the benefits & perks we offer, please visit here. 

 Hiring Range:
 $152,000 — $228,000 USD 

 We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. 

 If you need a reasonable accommodation, please contact us at accommodations@relativityspace.com . 

 Please note: Relativity Space does not accept unsolicited resumes, candidate profiles, or referrals from recruitment agencies or search firms. Any unsolicited submission - via email, our website, social media, or directly to an employee - will be deemed the property of Relativity Space, and no fee will be owed absent a current, fully executed agreement with Talent Acquisition that specifically authorizes submissions for the applicable role.

jobs.desc:
Join Komatsu and Be Part of Something Big! 
 Job Overview 

 Complete in a timely manner Manufacturing Engineering related projects with emphasis on safe work practices, Production/Warehouse Department procedures, routings, packaging requirements, manpower requirements, standards, layout, tooling/fixtures, equipment purchases that provide method improvements and cost reduction opportunities. Projects will include improved process flow in the fabrication/warehouse through shipping operations as well as supporting material flow and systems from suppliers to line side delivery. Programming CNC machines, fabricating, welding, painting, and assembly part knowledge with experience to develop processes to produce a part per print. Understand all warehouse processes through inbound packaging, put away, picking, packing, and shipping. Purpose of this position is to support and foster continuous improvement of all aspects of the Production/Warehouse Process. 

 Recommends tooling, equipment and system purchases to support current and new models along with warehouse processing of spare parts.  

 Responsible for generating routings, procedures, tool specifications and programs for automated equipment to meet SQDC demands. 

 Review layouts for continuous improvement and develop standards for all processes with manufacturing and warehouse operations.  

 Key Job Responsibilities 

 Select tools and programs related to automated equipment, such as CNC machine tools by utilizing CAD/CAM and computer software to effectively utilize manpower, machines, and facilities. 

 Complete projects assigned timely by utilizing project planning tools and communicating with all aspects required to successfully complete each project. 

 Recommends tooling, equipment to assist Fabrication and Warehousing through confirmation process flow for existing Models and revised and/or new Models along with warehouse processes. 

 Update Production routings to coordinate fabrication through assembly flow, include confirmation and report proper costing and coordinate introduction of ECN’s (Engineering Change Notices). Setup operations within MRP system to manage inventory for warehouse. 

 Develop Manpower requirements for area assigned of the Production Department to support changing production volumes and assist with proper manning levels. Including Warehouse Department.

 Bachelor of Science Degree in Manufacturing or Industrial Engineering. 

 Minimum of 1 to 3 years of experience in the manufacturing engineering field. 

 Proficient with all computer applications, i.e. Excel, Word, Power Point, Project Management etc.

jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer-Programmer lll
jobs.desc:
Join Komatsu and Be Part of Something Big! 
 Job Overview 

 The Manufacturing Engineer/Programmer III provides technical manufacturing engineering and CNC programming support for machining operations, with a focus on improving safety, quality, productivity, cost, and on-time delivery. This role analyzes drawings, specifications, sketches, and design data to develop manufacturing processes, create and maintain CNC programs, select tooling and fixtures, establish speeds and feeds, and document setup sheets and process instructions for boring bars and horizontal machining centers.

 This position works closely with manufacturing, engineering, quality, safety, purchasing, suppliers, supervisors, and hourly production employees to support production needs, troubleshoot issues, improve machining methods, and implement cost-effective manufacturing solutions. The role also supports capital projects, evaluates tooling and equipment needs, assists with routings, PFMEAs, cost estimates, and provides hands-on technical guidance to operators. Success in this role requires strong machining knowledge, experience with Mastercam, SolidWorks, and machine controls such as Fanuc or Siemens, along with the ability to manage multiple projects, communicate clearly, and actively support a safe manufacturing environment.

 Key Job Responsibilities 

• Provides technical assistance to Manufacturing Engineering and Manufacturing organization. 

• Analyzes drawings, sketches, and design data of part to determine dimension and configuration of cuts. Creates and maintains programs which includes selecting fixturing and cutting tools, and machine speeds and feeds; and creates process sheets and tooling lists for Boring Bar and Horizontal Machining Centers. 

• Is a resource for capital projects.  May prepare appropriation requests for capital projects 

• Identifies opportunities for process improvements and carries out improvement actions. 

• Develops new and improved manufacturing methods (DFMA). 

• Identifies opportunities to reduce cost, improve productivity, safety, quality, velocity, OTD, etc. 

 Qualifications/Requirements 

• Minimum 4 years manufacturing experience 

• BS Engineering (Mechanical, Manufacturing, Industrial).  Would consider equivalent from two-year college or technical school; and Journeyman’s status or 5 years of experience in the machining trades or equivalent. 

• Familiar with a variety of field concepts, practices, and procedures. 

• Relies on extensive experience and judgement to plan and accomplish goals. 

• Familiar with large equipment and parts 

• Language Ability: Ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedure manuals. Ability to write necessary correspondence. Ability to speak effectively before groups of customers or employees of organization. 

 Safety

• Promote and support a safety-first culture by designing, improving, and sustaining manufacturing processes that protect employees, reduce risk, and support safe work execution.

• Incorporate Komatsu safety goals, policies, and cardinal safety expectations into engineering decisions, process improvements, equipment layouts, tooling changes, and standard work.

• Partner with operations, safety, quality, maintenance, and production teams to identify hazards, assess risk, and implement corrective actions that improve employee safety and operational performance.

• Actively support continuous improvement initiatives that reduce unsafe conditions, improve ergonomics, eliminate waste, and strengthen reliable day-to-day work practices.

• Ensure engineering recommendations consider safe material flow, machine guarding, crane and forklift movement, work-at-height exposure, suspended loads, pinch points, and other shop-floor risks.

• Participate in safety reviews, incident investigations, root cause analysis, and corrective action planning as needed to prevent recurrence and improve future processes.

jobs.desc:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known. 

 Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us. 

 About the Team: 

 The Propulsion Manufacturing Integrated Components team manufactures and tests critical Aeon-R engine components including manifolds, gimbal assemblies, brackets, orifices, etc. The team ensures on-time delivery of propulsion subassemblies to the Aeon-R engine program while driving continuous improvements in safety, quality, reliability, lead time, and cost. 

 After successfully delivering hardware and developing processes for the first Aeon-R flight engines, we're entering a critical phase: ramping production while concurrently developing next-generation engines to make Terran R the most manufacturable high-performing rocket to date. This role requires a high degree of autonomy and initiative to provide design feedback, pioneer advanced manufacturing methods, and deliver flight hardware for integration and testing. 

 About the Role: 

• Own and develop manufacturing and test processes for 3D printed and machined Aeon-R engine components and subassemblies 

• Drive continuous improvements in manufacturability, assembly, and delivery of components, ensuring hardware meets all aspects of the intended design 

• Collaborate with manufacturing partners and technicians by writing work instructions, conducting root cause analysis, resolving issues, and tracking and reducing lead time 

• Partner with supply chain to develop and manage external supplier relationships, ensuring on-time hardware delivery 

• Work hands-on in a fast-paced, often novel, high-mix environment while collaborating cross-functionally and driving projects to completion 

• Build a strong manufacturing team and lead projects directly and cross-functionally 

 About You: 

• Bachelor’s degree in engineering or related technical field and 2+ years of relevant experience in manufacturing engineering or a related role. 

• Strong foundational knowledge of propulsion systems, mechanics of materials, and thermal-fluid systems to investigate and resolve hardware defects 

• Ability to work with and train technicians in a hands-on hardware environment, writing work instructions, and process plans for complex assemblies, and drive implementation of improvement and corrective actions 

• Vendor management experience including selection, defect disposition, and quality management 

• Proficiency with additive/subtractive manufacturing, precision inspection, GD&T (ASME Y14.5), and FEA using Ansys or similar tools 

• Experience with tooling design using Siemens NX or other CAD tools, including conceptualization, modeling, analysis, and fabrication 

 Nice to haves but not required: 

• Experience in propulsion development programs 

• Experience transitioning products from development to high-volume production

jobs.title: Lead Engineer, GSE and Production Tooling
jobs.desc:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB 

 Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

 LEAD ENGINEER, GSE AND PRODUCTION TOOLING 

 We are currently seeking a Lead Engineer for our Tooling, Test, and Infrastructure team based out of Rocket Lab's newest Space Structures Complex production facility in Middle River, MD. The Lead Engineer will be responsible for the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of tooling, GSE, and test for the Neutron Launch Vehicle.  

 WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO:   

 Manage a team of Engineers responsible for tooling, GSE, and test for Neutron 

 Coordinate a team focused on: 

• Production tooling: how we massively scale the production of Neutron and create mechanical tools which allow us to increase assembly accuracy, reduce set-up times, minimize crane use, etc. 

• Ground Support Equipment: design of equipment that interfaces with the vehicle for test, transport, and integration 

• Test: engineering coordination of qual tests and structural tests. 

 Coordinate with structures team, other Lead Engineers, facilities, operations, and other major stakeholders to: 

• Manage facility-wide constraints 

• Develop appropriate training plans to ensure technicians are qualified to perform the expected tasks 

• Major capital projects to introduce new production techniques as we scale production 

• Contribute to design reviews acting as an expert in design for manufacture, design for test, productivity, supplier capability assessments, quality control, etc. 

 In addition, the Lead Engineer will perform the following tasks in a leadership capacity: 

• Develop and mentor less experienced engineers and technicians 

• Ensure robust planning, including project schedules 

• Performance management for engineers on the team 

• Recruiting where needed for additional engineers 

 YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS:   

• Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, aerospace, or manufacturing engineering, or other technical degree. 

• 5 + years of engineering design experience.  

• Experience in a leadership position.

 THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE:   

• Demonstrated experience with large tooling and structures design  

• Working knowledge of Siemens NX/Teamcenter     

• Familiarity with manufacturing processes such as metallic machining, welding, and fabrication. 

• Experience with structural analysis including hand calcs and FEA

• Ability to read and interpret P&ID’s and wiring diagrams. 

• Demonstrated leadership competencies, especially change management, conflict resolution, knowing when to escalate / request help, effectively manage a team

 ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS 

• Sit at desk and operate computer, keyboard and office equipment for extended periods 

• Use hands with dexterity to operate controls, tools and technical equipment, as needed 

• Read technical documents, drawings, and computer screens requiring close and distance vision 

• Move between buildings, labs, and work areas, as needed 

• Work in office and technical environments with occasional exposure to noise, dust and fumes in production areas. 

 Anticipated annual equity grant value is designed around function, level, experience, and other factors; realized value depends on vesting and stock-price performance. 

 Join one of the world's fastest-growing space companies and own a piece of it. In addition to competitive base pay, you'll receive company stock as part of your total compensation package , giving you a direct stake in our success. As we expand to new launch sites, groundbreaking missions, and global markets, your ownership has the opportunity to grow alongside the company. 

 Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top tier medical HMO, PPO & a 100% company-sponsored medical HSA plan option, dental and vision coverage, 3 weeks paid vacation and 5 days sick leave per year, 11 paid holidays per year, flexible spending and dependent care savings accounts, paid parental leave, disability insurance, life insurance, access to a 401(k) retirement plan with company match, and free snacks/drinks onsite. 

 Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience. 

 Total Compensation (base and equity)
 $137,075 — $196,275 USD 

 Base Salary
 $116,800 — $160,600 USD 

 WHAT TO EXPECT 

 We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.

jobs.title: Process Engineer (Starship)
jobs.desc:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

 PROCESS ENGINEER (STARSHIP) 

 As a Process Engineer with a focus on Starship build reliability, you will be part of a widely interdisciplinary team developing global manufacturing procedures, maximizing quality through efficient production. You will employ “reliability by any means necessary”, stretching your expertise in fabrication methods, work instructions, tooling design, inspection procedures, data gathering/visualization, and broad collaboration. You will build new processes from the ground up, and routinely grade/improve execution of existing processes, driving continuous production improvement and ultimately be responsible for build-induced vehicle risk.

 RESPONSIBILITIES: 

• Develop manufacturing, integration, assembly, welding, NDE, cleanliness, and checkouts processes from the ground up, then enforce consistency across different work centers.

• Design and implement tooling for work access, mechanical/avionics/propulsion testing, build fixturing, lifting & rigging, and fluids.

• Define and document inspection requirements and procedures.

• Create training for production and inspection processes.

• Author planning, test plans, and training to execute processes and collect data, ensuring efficient and stable quality at increasing production volumes.

• Contain non-conforming hardware in collaboration with quality, production, and design groups to ensure systemic issues are corrected, and risk is managed for the fleet.

• Work closely with design teams to improve DFM and requirement fulfillment. Aggressively modify requirements and manufacturing process where design intent and production rate are incompatible.

• Conduct build quality reviews to identify repeat and high impact issues. Drive corrective action within and outside of your work center.

 BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: 

• Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, materials engineering, manufacturing engineering, chemical engineering, electrical engineering, or engineering physics.

• 1+ years in manufacturing, quality, and/or design engineering role (student project team or internship experience qualifies).

 PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: 

• Experience with the build, assembly, or integration of structures, avionics, valves, fluid system components, actuators, thermal protection systems, or other aerospace components.

• Mechanical tooling or component design and design for manufacturability.

• Proficiency with 3D CAD Software such as NX, SolidWorks, or CATIA.

• Knowledge of mig, tig, laser, stud, spot, or robot welding techniques, as well as visual, penetrant, x-ray, EMAT, or other NDT processes.

• Involvement in a collegiate or hobby design project (Formula SAE, rocketry, etc).

• Proficiency with SQL and Power BI or other database/query/data visualization suite.

• You thrive in a hands-on environment and are hungry to step out of the office, onto the shop floor.

• Knowledge of metallic manufacturing techniques, processes, and equipment related to machining, bending, forming, casting, additive manufacturing, fastening, drilling, and/or bonding.

• Strong interpersonal skills and ability to collaborate with partners/customers from a diverse set of engineering disciplines.

• Ability to work extended hours, weekends, and offsite as needed.

jobs.title: Prototype Manufacturing Engineer, Mechanical & Fluid Systems
jobs.desc:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE TEAM

 Anduril's Air Dominance & Strike (AD&S) Manufacturing Engineering team is seeking a Prototype Manufacturing Engineer to execute first builds and prototype manufacturing across our mechanical, structural, thermal management, and fluid systems (fuel, hydraulics, pneumatics) subsystems. This role spans the full AD&S portfolio of autonomous aircraft, cruise missiles, and loitering munitions – and is designed for an engineer who thrives in ambiguity, builds hardware with incomplete inputs, and treats every first build as an opportunity to generate the manufacturing knowledge that makes future production possible.

As a Prototype ME, you are the first manufacturing engineer on a new build. You will work from incomplete design definitions – often without released drawings or established work instructions – to figure out how hardware goes together, build the first units, and document what you learn. Your output is not just a built prototype; it is the MVP work instructions, preliminary BOM structure, buildability feedback, and lessons learned that the DFx and SME teams use to drive producibility improvements and prepare for rate production. You are the bridge between a design engineer's intent and the physical reality of how something gets built for the first time.

This is a cross-program role. You will move between AD&S programs based on where first builds are happening, bringing a consistent methodology to new hardware regardless of the product line. You will work closely with design engineers, DFx engineers, SME manufacturing engineers, and production technicians. The pace is fast, the inputs are messy, and the expectation is that you bring order to chaos – one build at a time.

 WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Execute first builds of new mechanical, structural, thermal, and fluid system hardware across AD&S programs, working from preliminary or incomplete design inputs (unreleased models, draft drawings, verbal direction from design engineers).

• Develop MVP work instructions during and immediately after first builds – capturing assembly sequences, tooling needs, critical dimensions, torque values, and process notes sufficient for a technician to repeat the build.

• Establish preliminary BOM structures (Make/Buy determinations) based on first-build experience, identifying which components should be fabricated internally, procured, or sent to contract manufacturers.

• Provide structured design feedback to design engineers based on first-build observations – specifically addressing buildability, checkability (can you inspect it?), and repeatability (can someone else build it the same way?).

• Document lessons learned from every first build and feed them directly to DFx engineers for incorporation into formal DFM/DFA reviews and design trade studies.

• Build and support Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) units – Ironbirds, Copperbirds, and similar integration test articles – where the build method is undefined and must be figured out from scratch.

• Identify and resolve manufacturing issues in real time on the shop floor during first builds, including fit/interference problems, fastener access issues, routing conflicts, and assembly sequence challenges.

• Develop or source prototype tooling, fixtures, and assembly aids needed for first builds – balancing speed with enough rigor that the tooling concept can inform production tooling decisions later.

• Work with SME manufacturing engineers to validate process assumptions – confirming that the manufacturing processes assumed in design (welding methods, composite layup approaches, tube forming techniques, adhesive bonding sequences) are feasible as designed.

• Support the transition of hardware from prototype to early production by ensuring first-build documentation, lessons learned, and BOM structures are complete and transferred to the product-owning ME team.

• Collaborate with quality engineering to identify inspection points and acceptance criteria that emerge from first-build experience – particularly for characteristics not yet captured in drawings or specifications.

• Travel to production sites, supplier facilities, and integration locations to support first builds and prototype campaigns (~15-20%, depending on program needs).

 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related field.

• 5+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering, prototype/development manufacturing, or NPI with hands-on involvement in building new hardware – not just sustaining existing production lines.

• Demonstrated experience executing first builds or first-article production of mechanical or electromechanical hardware with incomplete or evolving design inputs.

• Practical knowledge of mechanical manufacturing and assembly processes: CNC machining, sheet metal fabrication, welding, mechanical fastening, composite fabrication, tube bending/swaging, adhesive bonding, and mechanical integration.

• Ability to read mechanical drawings, interpret GD&T, and work from 3D models – and the judgment to know when something in the model won't work on the shop floor.

• Experience writing work instructions, assembly procedures, or process documen

 Qualifications/Requirements 

• Bachelor of Science degree in Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a closely related engineering discipline.

• Specific and demonstrated experience with understanding, developing and driving manufacturing improvements through design, manufacturing and process improvement projects.

• Proficient with all computer applications, i.e. Excel, Word, Power Point, Project Management etc.

• Patience, persistence, and problem-solving skills are very important.

About Lucid 

 At Lucid, we are creating exceptional mobility experiences through innovation to drive the world forward. Built on Lucid’s proprietary technology and software-defined vehicle architecture, our award-winning vehicles bring our “Compromise Nothing™” approach to the global automotive market. That means refusing to choose between performance and sustainability, design and engineering, ambition and integrity. In Lucid Air and Lucid Gravity, we have designed and built vehicles that have redefined their segments, combining exceptional range, performance, design, and expansive space in a single experience. 

 We achieve this through deep vertical integration, with design, engineering, and production happening in-house across our global offices and manufacturing facilities.  The General Assembly Advanced Manufacturing Engineering team enables Lucid to launch safe, efficient, production-ready assembly processes at scale. jobs.title: Senior Manufacturing Engineer, Integrated Components
jobs.desc:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known. 

 Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us. 

 About the Team: 

 The Propulsion Manufacturing Integrated Components team manufactures and tests critical Aeon-R engine components including manifolds, gimbal assemblies, brackets, orifices, etc. The team ensures on-time delivery of propulsion subassemblies to the Aeon-R engine program while driving continuous improvements in safety, quality, reliability, lead time, and cost. 

 After successfully delivering hardware and developing processes for the first Aeon-R flight engines, we're entering a critical phase: ramping production while concurrently developing next-generation engines to make Terran R the most manufacturable high-performing rocket to date. This role requires a high degree of autonomy and initiative to provide design feedback, pioneer advanced manufacturing methods, and deliver flight hardware for integration and testing. 

 About the Role: 

• Own and develop manufacturing and test processes for 3D printed and machined Aeon-R engine components and subassemblies 

• Drive continuous improvements in manufacturability, assembly, and delivery of components, ensuring hardware meets all aspects of the intended design 

• Collaborate with manufacturing partners and technicians by writing work instructions, conducting root cause analysis, resolving issues, and tracking and reducing lead time 

• Partner with supply chain to develop and manage external supplier relationships, ensuring on-time hardware delivery 

• Work hands-on in a fast-paced, often novel, high-mix environment while collaborating cross-functionally and driving projects to completion 

• Build a strong manufacturing team and lead projects directly and cross-functionally 

 About You: 

• Bachelor’s degree in engineering or related technical field and 5+ years of relevant experience in manufacturing engineering or a related role. 

• Strong foundational knowledge of propulsion systems, mechanics of materials, and thermal-fluid systems to investigate and resolve hardware defects 

• Ability to work with and train technicians in a hands-on hardware environment, writing work instructions, and process plans for complex assemblies, and drive implementation of improvement and corrective actions 

• Vendor management experience including selection, defect disposition, and quality management 

• Proficiency with additive/subtractive manufacturing, precision inspection, GD&T (ASME Y14.5), and FEA using Ansys or similar tools 

• Experience with tooling design using Siemens NX or other CAD tools, including conceptualization, modeling, analysis, and fabrication 

 Nice to haves but not required: 

• Experience in propulsion development programs 

• Experience transitioning products from development to high-volume production 

• Hands-on experience with CNC machining, welding, and high-pressure testing 

• Experience writing formal process specifications and manufacturing standards

Job Description Summary 
The Lead Manufacturing Engineer – Fabrication Manufacturing Readiness supports the design, sourcing, and production of complex aerospace components and assemblies for Edison Works Advanced Programs. In this role, you will drive design for manufacturing readiness, producibility, reduce manufacturing cost and risk, and ensure our suppliers along with internal GE shops can deliver safely, on quality, on time, and at cost — with a specific focus on fabrication technologies.

* Drive manufacturing readiness for complex fabrication processes (e.g., machining, forming, welding, additive manufacturing) from concept through production launch.
* Collaborate with design engineering, supply chain, and quality teams to ensure design for manufacturability (DFM) and assembly (DFA).
* Develop and implement robust manufacturing plans, including process flow, equipment selection, tooling requirements, and facility layouts.
* Lead technical reviews and provide expertise on fabrication process capabilities, limitations, and best practices.
* Conduct process capability studies, root cause analysis, and implement corrective actions for manufacturing issues.
* Identify and implement advanced manufacturing technologies and automation solutions to improve efficiency and reduce costs.
* Develop and manage project schedules and budgets for manufacturing readiness activities.
* Mentor and provide technical guidance to junior engineers and manufacturing personnel.
* Ensure compliance with all relevant safety, quality, and regulatory standards.
* Travel as required to support manufacturing sites and suppliers.

Job Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
* Minimum of 3 years of experience in manufacturing engineering within a fabrication environment, preferably in aerospace or a highly regulated industry.
* Proven experience leading manufacturing readiness projects for new product introductions.
* Strong understanding of various fabrication processes, such as CNC machining, sheet metal forming, welding, brazing, and/or additive manufacturing.
* Proficiency in CAD/CAM software (e.g., NX, CATIA, Mastercam).
* Demonstrated ability to apply Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma methodologies.
* Excellent project management, problem-solving, and analytical skills.
* Strong communication, interpersonal, and leadership abilities, with the capacity to influence cross-functional teams.
* Ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

jobs.desc:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 Anduril’s Manufacturing team is seeking a Manufacturing Engineer to join our team to support AeroStructures branch in North Carolina . This Manufacturing Team is responsible for rapidly iterating and building cutting-edge aerostructure assemblies, starting from the piece part manufacturing. This role encompasses everything in the manufacturing value-chain, including, but not limited to, MBOM Management, Work Instruction creation, Design for Manufacturability work, work cell optimization, tool design & selection, process creation & optimization, vendor sourcing & interaction, quality planning, and work documentation associated with the composite and metallic structures.

 The right person for this role can demonstrate experience in composite part manufacturing and overall airframe assembly. This person will also demonstrate the ability to work across multiple functions (Manufacturing Operations, Airframe Design, Quality, Leadership, Supply Chain, etc) to achieve a successful manufacturing approach, flow, and build.

 WHAT YOU’LL DO 

• Work with technicians and other engineers hands-on, building composite parts and tooling in close conjunction with design engineering release

• Write manufacturing documentation, such as work instructions, MBOMs, quality plans, inspection requirements, non-conformances, while also completing said work instructions, quality plans, and inspections alongside a team of technicians and inspectors

• Work as a conduit between the engineering technical data packages and the technicians to ensure composite hardware and tooling are manufactured as designed/analyzed

• Solve manufacturing problems in schedule-driven environment under the constraints of detailed specifications and requirements to achieve the needed quality, delivered on schedule

• Drive work cell design and optimization to ensure quality and efficiency targets are maintained and managed

• Work with the Program Managers to inform critical decision points to ensure on-time delivery

• Drive RCCAs alongside the quality team to eliminate production blockers and recurring issues

 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 

• 2+ years of experience in a relevant field, preferably manufacturing or design of composite parts and/or assemblies

• A genuine interest in manufacturing and thirst for learning

• Experience with MS Office and/or project management software skills

• Eligible to obtain and maintain an Active T.S. Clearance

• Experience supporting aerospace, defense, automotive, and/or energetics facilities

• Experience working within a AS9100/NADCAP accredited manufacturing facility

• Proficiency in TeamCenter for digital manufacturing processes

• Composite and Metallic Airframe assembly processes

• Understanding of CNC Machining operation and limitations – 5-axis routers, lathes, mills, etc

• Bachelor’s degree in an engineering or technology related field

At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known. 

 Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us. 

 About the team: 

 The Manufacturing team at Relativity Space is currently deep in manufacturing trades and process development for Terran R, our next generation, fully re-useable rocket. This team has a wide variety of responsibilities—from determining the most efficient factory floor layout, to developing and implementing complex tooling and processes, and even interfacing with the vehicle engineering team to heavily influence the design of the rocket. Unique to Relativity, you will get to work across many teams to iterate and support development of the vehicle program. 

 About the role: 

• Own a major primary structure assembly and its child subassemblies (landing legs, grid fins, tank structures, thrust structure, interstage, payload adapters, or heatshield components) from first build into rate production 

• Generate and maintain the mBOM, CONOPS, and build schedule throughout the development process 

• Create work instructions, specifications, and best practices across multiple high-fidelity processes, and help standardize those processes across the manufacturing team 

• Help establish the stations within the inaugural work cell, accounting for assembly operations, tooling and capital equipment requirements, and rate targets 

• Support the shop floor through live issue resolution, and drive process improvements and lessons learned back into the production flow and into the next generation of manufacturing technology 

• Provide Design for Manufacturing feedback to the structures teams through the first prototype and flight builds, working closely with design, manufacturing, and reliability engineers, internal production teams, external vendors, and Factory Development 

 About You: 

• Bachelor’s degree in aeronautical, mechanical engineering, or other engineering discipline 

• 1+ years progressive and related experience required 

• Excellent interpersonal skills with the ability to interface with engineering and manufacturing groups to understand process constraints and provide design inputs for improved manufacturability 

• Working knowledge of primary vehicle structures, machining, assembly process, & tooling - Intermediate to Advanced knowledge of GD&T 

• Ability to perform trade studies using first principles and engineering fundamentals 

• Able to work well in an integrated collaborative team environment 

• Highly self-motivated and able to prioritize and execute tasks in a high-pressure environment 

 Nice to Have: 

• Experience transitioning products from prototype to mass production 

• New product introduction of an aerospace hardware system into a manufacturing, test, and production system with proven success 

• Experience in managing projects in a fast-paced environment 

• Experience with critical lifting and tool design to support urgent operations 

• Experience welding high temp alloys 

• Experience with full size determinate assembly (FSDA)

jobs.desc:

Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us. 

 About the Team: 

 The Stage Manufacturing team turns design into reality, owning the build of Terran R’s primary structures. This isn’t about turning the same bolt every day; it’s about building the systems to build the rocket. Engineers and technicians work side by side, with deep collaboration and real-time feedback, to shape how we build better and faster. With a manifest and a launch date, it’s up to the team to deliver on Terran R: solving challenges in real time, optimizing for scale, and constantly improving processes. As the vehicle evolves, so will the factory, with opportunities to apply automation, machine learning, and advanced technologies. What we build here sets the blueprint for the future of scaled launch. 

 About the Role: 

• Own hardware from design release through build, test, and delivery for engine or vehicle systems, taking full responsibility for execution readiness and product quality across subassemblies and integrated systems

• Develop and release detailed build flows, work instructions, and test procedures to enable repeatable, high-quality execution across first builds and maturing programs 

• Support first article builds in a fast-paced environment, focusing on manufacturability, repeatability, and quality, while developing scalable processes that enable a smooth ramp to higher production rates 

• Provide hands-on floor support during build and test, resolving issues in real time, incorporating technician feedback, and driving continuous improvement across hardware flow and process discipline 

• Coordinate across design, supply chain, production, and test teams to ensure part readiness, tooling availability, schedule alignment, and smooth handoffs between build stages 

• Contribute to the development of long-term manufacturing systems and infrastructure, including tooling strategies, ERP/MES workflows, and production documentation standards 

 About You: 

• Degree in engineering or a related technical field, with 2+ years of hands-on experience building and testing hardware in a manufacturing or integration environment 

• Skilled at investigating hardware issues, resolving non-conformances, and driving root cause analysis with corrective actions implemented effectively 

• Familiar with general assembly and test procedures, including tolerance stack-up analysis, structural proof testing, and pressurized leak checks 

• Comfortable interfacing across design, manufacturing, supply chain, and test teams to ensure hardware quality and schedule alignment 

• Self-starter who can define and roll out new processes from scratch, working collaboratively with technicians, engineers, and external vendors 

• Proficient in GD&T, CAD, and basic design or test analysis, with experience in at least two of the following: LOX cleanliness, leak checking, sensor checkouts, tube bending, tool design, crane operations, or subassembly builds 

 Nice to haves but not required: 

• Experience supporting new aerospace product introduction or transitioning hardware from prototype to production, especially in a high-rate or scaling environment 

• Experience directly authoring and executing test procedures, including acting as a test conductor for integrated system verification 

• Familiarity with hazardous operations, fluid system safety, or test execution involving pressurized or high-risk environments 

• Experience in a fast-paced and lean environment, including direct vendor engagement, tool development, or leading a small team through an ambiguous build or test effort

jobs.title: Tool Engineer/Principal Tool Engineer
jobs.desc:
RELOCATION ASSISTANCE: Relocation assistance may be available 

CLEARANCE REQUIRED FOR START: Yes 

CLEARANCE TYPE: Secret 

TRAVEL: Yes, 10% of the Time Description 

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history. 

 Northrop Grumman Aeronautics Systems sector is seeking a Tool Engineer or Principal Tool Engineer to join our team of qualified, diverse individuals located in Palmdale, CA .

 Duties Include: 
 • Coordination of design and fabrication requirements for tools and fixtures with customers, both internal and external

• Coordinate/develop & execute test plans

• Conduct root cause failure investigations and implement associated corrective actions

• Develop & evaluate process improvements

• Ensures adequate funding and performs schedule risk assessments to identify and mitigate program cost and schedule and technical risks

• Lead and manage all phases of project: design, documentation, fabrication, assembly, validation and sustainment

• Develop high-quality presentations for leadership meetings, workshops, and stakeholder briefings

• Present project updates effectively to leadership, ensuring clarity and alignment on project progress and next steps

 The Tool Engineer shall work with internal/external customers, and colleagues to ensure that the design meets the customer’s needs and see it through each phase of the engineering process (Design, Fabrication, and Implementation).

 Basic Qualifications for Tool Engineer: 
 • Bachelor’s degree with 1 year of technical and/or engineering experience or Master’s degree with 0 years of experience

• Ability to read, interpret, and analyze technical models and drawings

• Basic knowledge of geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T/ASME Y 14.5)

• Experience coordinating with cross functional teams across multiple organizations

• Experience with computer aided design tools and systems (e.g., computer aided design / computer aided manufacturing CAD/CAM)

• Experience managing projects (Cost, schedule and technical performance)

• This position requires an active in-scope U.S. Government Secret security clearance that has been granted / renewed within the past 5 years and ability to maintain

• Must have the ability to obtain and maintain Special Program Access within a reasonable period of time, as determined by the company to meet its business needs

 WHAT YOU’LL DO 

 As a Mechanical Design Engineer focused on DFM/DFA , you will sit at the critical intersection of product design and production reality. You will be directly responsible for designing robust, mission-ready, and highly manufacturable hardware across Anduril’s portfolio of autonomous air, land, and maritime systems. You will own components and assemblies from concept through prototype fabrication and high-rate production, ensuring our hardware can be rapidly built, scaled, and deployed at the speed of mission need.

• Complex weldments and welded joint architecture

jobs.title: Mechanical Design Engineer, Hardware Platform, 2+ years of experience
jobs.desc:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE TEAM 

 The Hardware Platform Organization is Anduril's central hardware engineering org. We build the shared technologies, tools, and infrastructure that power hardware development across every Anduril division, from actuators and propulsion to batteries, avionics, rocket motors, and test operations. Our teams set engineering standards, run development manufacturing and test sites, and develop core technology products that ship across multiple product lines.

 ABOUT THE ROLE

 Anduril is seeking exceptional, hands-on Mechanical Design Engineers to design, test, and scale mission-critical hardware across our autonomous air, sea, ground, and strike platforms. 

 We are hiring across three core work-streams. Depending on your background, technical depth, and career focus, you will align with one of the following hardware teams:

• Core Technology Products: Architect foundational hardware platforms spanning aircraft, missiles, maritime vessels, and ground systems. You will lead blank-sheet mechanical packaging, tight electro-mechanical integration (thermal, RF, PCBAs), and rapid hardware iteration.

• Lethality (Warhead Design): Design and mature advanced warheads, ordnance, and munitions systems. You will bridge mechanical engineering, dynamic modeling, energetic material packaging, safety constraints, and live-fire test operations.

• Design for Excellence (DFM / DFA): Sit at the critical interface between initial CAD concepts and production reality. You will drive high-rate manufacturability, assembly optimization, drawing standards, and tooling strategies to ensure hardware can scale at the speed of mission need.

 WHAT YOU’LL DO 

• End-to-End Hardware Ownership: Own components and complex mechanical assemblies from requirements definition, hand calculations, and conceptual design through prototyping, testing, and volume manufacturing.

• Rigorous Mechanical Design: Create high-fidelity 3D models and fully defined 2D drawing packages in strict accordance with ASME Y14.5 (GD&T) standards.

• Multi-Discipline Engineering: Design parts across diverse fabrication processes—including precision 3/5-axis CNC machining, complex weldments, sheet metal, injection molding, composite layups, and structural adhesive bonding.

 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 The Structures and Mechanisms team is responsible for the full design, build, and test lifecycle of Terran R’s integrated structures and flight mechanisms. Both teams fall under one department, sharing design principles, tools, and an integrated approach that provides a comprehensive view of Terran R. Beyond first flight, you’ll play a critical role in refining for manufacturability and speed. 

 About the Role: 

• The scope of work encompasses designing parts and systems from early conceptualization through full release and supporting manufacturing for primary and secondary structures related to all stages of the Terran R rocket. You will need to think creatively and leverage innovation to optimize part geometry, ensure assembly packaging, prevent interferences and excessive gapping, reduce mass, and make parts fully manufacturable. You’ll also assist manage parts and assemblies throughout their lifecycles in PLM, and you’ll control BOM structuring and configuration management for many systems across the vehicle. • Perform packaging assessment of systems – resolve interferences, perform tolerance stack analyses, validate hardware stacks and fastener selections, integrate nominal gapping and shimming strategies, and more 

• Support BOM and configuration management of various systems across multiple vehicles

Ideally, you have significant mechanical or structural design experience and a proven track record completing collaborative projects effectively. 

• On a weekly basis, you will be designing flight components for our upcoming Terran R vehicle using NX/TeamCenter, creating and releasing drawings as well as supporting fabrication of your components. You will also use your strong organizational skills to properly document your work and present your recommendations when decisions are needed.

• Bachelor’s degree in engineering or a related discipline 

• Experience with industry-standard CAD packages such as NX, CATIA, Creo, or SOLIDWORKS

jobs.title: Rack Design Engineer (Starmind)
jobs.desc:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

 RACK DESIGN ENGINEER (STARMIND)

 The Starmind Compute team designs training and inference compute clusters from first principles, pushing thermal, electrical, and optical systems to the limit of physics. We operate as a highly cross disciplinary team comprised of mechanical, electrical, optical, and software engineers, all working to maximize the efficiency, reliability, and deployment speed of terrestrial computing to serve rapidly scaling demand.

 This team owns compute architecture, datacenter network design, rack builds, connectivity, in-house design of our own computers, and the manufacturing line that builds that compute. As a Rack Design Engineer, you will own the rack as a product: structure, power, cooling, service paths, and the physical integration of servers, switches, optics, and liquid cooling from first sketch through production rate.

 RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Own mechanical, structural, and integration design of high-density AI compute racks and associated chassis, frames, busbars, manifolds, and cable/fiber raceways

• Integrate compute, networking, power distribution, and liquid cooling into a buildable, serviceable, high-yield rack architecture

• Design for the in-house manufacturing line: DFM/DFA, fixtures, work instructions, incoming inspection, first article, and production ramp

• Close thermal, structural, and power constraints with cooling, electrical, optical, and network counterparts at the cluster level (CDUs, cold plates, quick disconnects, PDUs/busbars, high-current distribution, tray and bend-radius limits)

• Drive vendor and in-house parts from concept to qualified production, including sheet metal, extrusions, busbar, manifolds, cable management, and rack accessories

• Stand on the floor during prototype and production builds: debug fit, leak, cable dress, airflow/liquid balance, and service time; fold issues into the next revision the same day

• Produce and maintain CAD, BOMs, drawings, and build documentation that a line can run at volume

• Support cluster deployment of the racks you design, including first-site bring-up and feedback into the next hardware generation

• Partner with network, optical, electrical, and firmware teams to deploy custom compute for inference and training across SpaceX programs

 BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, or another engineering discipline

• 2+ years of professional experience designing electromechanical hardware that was built and shipped (internship and project experience counts toward this if the hardware was physically produced)

 PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Ownership of rack, chassis, or similarly dense electromechanical products through prototype and production

• Experience or background in ethernet switching, networking, interconnects, high power distribution, and other relevant data center technologies 

• CAD fluency in SolidWorks, Creo, or NX, with released drawings a shop and a factory can build from

• AI / HPC / GPU rack design: NVIDIA HGX/GB-class, custom OCP, or equivalent high-power liquid-cooled compute

• Liquid cooling design: cold plates, manifolds, CDUs, quick disconnects, leak detection, and coolant compatibility

• High-power rack electrical integration: busbar, PDU, 48V, high-current 3-phase, grounding, and service safety

• Cable and fiber physical design inside the rack (MPO/OSFP dress, bend radius, service loops) in partnership with optical and network engineers

• Experience taking a rack from NPI onto an in-house manufacturing line (fixtures, cycle time, poka-yoke, rework loops)

• Thermal and structural analysis (CFD, FEA) used to make a design decision

• Time at a high-velocity hardware organization: AI/GPU cloud, custom compute, or an OEM/ODM team that owned the product end to end

• Comfort in a factory or datacenter build environment, including first articles, yield, and hardware debug on the floor

 ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed to support design releases, line bring-up, and cluster deployments

• Must be willing to travel up to 30% to manufacturing and datacenter sites

• Ability to lift up to 25 lbs. unassisted and work around active factory and datacenter hardware

• Understanding of aerospace materials and assembly methods (bonding/fastening)
• Ability to perform design of complex, multi-piece tool assemblies to ensure successful execution of manufacturing and test plans
• Experience in CAD and PLM systems, such as Siemens NX and Teamcenter.

 Preferred Qualifications: 
 • Experience with aerospace tooling, including composite layup molds, precision assembly fixtures, and Ground Support Equipment (GSE)

• Demonstrated initiative and strong interpersonal skills, thriving both independently and collaboratively within a team environment
