jobs.desc:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB 

 Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

 SPACE SYSTEMS 

 At Rocket Lab, we’re not just launching rockets — we're building the future of space. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, like solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, and more.

 Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. The team has built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help them get to space — our world class Space Systems team is empowering some of the boldest and most ambitious space missions.

 SENIOR PRODUCTION ENGINEER I 

 Based out of Rocket Lab's s ite in Albuquerque, NM as part of the SolAero Technologies acquisition, the Senior Production Engineer I is responsible for developing and maintaining processes for building advanced solar panels for space applications and ensuring they won’t fail on orbit . You will support the Panel Engineering Manager and the Production organization , with deliverables required for internal leadership, board of directors, and investors. 

 WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO: 

• Function as the technical champion of our manufacturing processes, solving problems in real-time with the Operators and Technicians building spaceflight hardware 

• Be the liaison between the technical/process parts of the business and the operations/execution arm on the production floor 

• Proactively remove hurdles from those executing manufacturing processes and maintain an environment where manufacturing operators and technicians can excel. 

• Develop a practical understanding of the design, construction, manufacturing methods and operating principles of series interconnected multi-junction solar cells. 

• Develop a practical understanding of the effects that external variables such as temperature, strain conditions, and the effects of a space environment can have on the materials used in the manufacture of solar panels. 

• Develop a detailed understanding of parallel gap resistance welding, mechanical fixturing for high throughput assembly, and additive manufacturing techniques. 

• Develop a practical working knowledge of the dispense and cure of space grade polymeric adhesives, the methods by which they can be mixed, degassed, and applied. An understanding should be built about the methods by which these materials cure and the factors that drive the effectiveness and rate of that cure. 

• Develop a working knowledge of the electrical circuits used in solar panels and the design constraints thereof 

• Combine the understanding described above to support current manufacturing capability and work to monitor/improve/expand the existing processes by working with area engineers 

• Use your background with PLCs and process automation to support an automated assembly line 

• Use analysis tools such as Excel, JMP and presentation tools such as Word and PowerPoint to develop and present results of experiments that you may help execute to internal groups 

• Use your experience writing technical documents to help develop a set of standard work instructions for new automated manufacturing processes 

• Effectively train operators on the proper use of equipment, and support their work with proper guidance, expertise and help. Provide the daily support that these folks need to be successful. 

• Develop collaborative working relationships with operators, technicians, engineers, and managers.  

 YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS: 

• A Bachelor’s degree in a related technical field or sufficient equivalent experience. 

• 5+ years related experience supporting a manufacturing line in a technical role 

• Attention to detail and previous demonstrated experience with writing technical instruction documents 

 THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE: 

• E xperience working with PLC based systems or automated manufacturing tools 

• Experience designing tooling and mechanical solutions to support a manufacturing line or process 

• Experience with any programming or scripting is a plus, as is SQL experience 

• Experience using Statistical Process Control (SPC) to understand whether a process is performing as intended 

• Experience with parallel gap resistance welding, polymeric adhesives, wiring, or mechanical fixturing processes 

 This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas. 
 WHAT TO EXPECT 

 We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE TEAM

 Anduril is fielding the next generation of Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) to tackle the extremely challenging industry demands of seabed exploration. Anduril has brought to the market a unique, ultra-long-range, full-ocean-depth platform, and a completely refreshed maritime vehicle and flexible manufacturing architecture that scales from "large" to "extra-large" vehicle sizes. Today, Anduril is executing on multi-million-dollar contracts while simultaneously performing Robot-as-a-Service (RaaS) AUV operations.

 We are looking for a Manufacturing Engineer to join our growing team in Quonset, RI. • Work with technicians and other engineers in a hands-on fashion building prototype hardware

• Develop novel tooling solutions for fabrication and assembly of structural parts

• Personal experience physically manufacturing hardware via any means (machining, fabrication, soldering, assembly, etc.). Work on personal or extracurricular projects is a plus

• Extremely organized and detail-oriented

• Excellent verbal & written communication skills

• Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Experience in sub-sea robotics (AUVs, UUVs, underwater sensors/equipment)

• Experience working with electrical systems up to 400VDc

• Subsea cable splicing or fabrication experience

• Experience with pressure vessels and/or pressure systems/equipment

• Prior experience working with JIRA, Teamcenter (PLM), NetSuite (ERP) or equivalents

Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us. 

 About the Team: 

 The Manufacturing team owns all process development, fabrication strategy, and production equipment for Terran R, our next generation, reusable rocket. This team has a wide variety of responsibilities – from factory floor layout, to developing complex tooling for novel processes, and interfacing with our vehicle engineering team to heavily influence design of the rocket. We leverage our deep expertise to translate engineering requirements into highly optimized production lines, working cross functionally to consistently enhance the vehicle program. 

 About the Role: 

• Own the application of Paint and Thermal Protection System materials from design release through successful installation onto the Terran R launch vehicle—lay out the build flow to ensure an efficient, high-quality process capable of scaling production rate with time 

• Drive first build efforts and improve existing product lines through design integration, assembly sequencing, mBOM development, build work order creation, and specification authoring 

• Support the shop floor and production personnel through responsive issue resolution and provide upstream feedback as we innovate the next generation of manufacturing technology 

• Monitor large scale part movements and ensure safety through clear and concise direction 

• Develop strong working relationships with Engineering, Build Reliability, Supply Chain, and external partners to ensure all company objectives can be met 

 About You: 

• Bachelor’s degree in aeronautical, mechanical engineering, or other engineering discipline with 1-2 years progressive and related work experience 

• 3D & 2D design/drafting working experience per ASME Y14.5M (NX preferred) 

• Excellent interpersonal skills with the ability to interface with engineering and manufacturing groups to understand process constraints and provide design inputs for improved manufacturability 

• Working experience with at least 2 of the following processes: adhesive bonding, soft goods manufacturing, coating processes, machining, mechanical fastening and torquing operations, trim and drill operations, composites manufacturing, critical lifting, tool design and fabrication, work center development 

• Ability to perform trade studies using first principles and engineering fundamentals 

• Highly self-motivated and able to prioritize and execute tasks in a high-pressure environment 

 Nice to haves but not required: 

• New product introduction of an aerospace hardware product or process with proven success 

• Experience in managing multiple projects in a fast-paced environment 

• Working knowledge of typical manufacturing execution systems and quality management systems 

• Master’s degree in engineering or related technical discipline

jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer (Raptor Combustion Devices Machining)
jobs.desc:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

 MANUFACTURING ENGINEER (RAPTOR COMBUSTION DEVICES MACHINING) 

 As a Manufacturing Engineer for Raptor machining, you will have the opportunity to influence, scale, and solve challenging problems relating to the production of Raptor machined piece parts and processing. The ideal candidate will thrive in a fast-paced environment with ever-changing scope and focus areas. This individual understands how to best design for manufacturing and will conceptualize/implement full-scale production processes for machining our critical hardware within production rate and cost goals. 

 RESPONSIBILITIES: 

• Identify, develop, and implement machining processes to help solve for engine cost, quality, and production rate – specifically focused on valve, turbopump, thrust chamber or injector hardware.

• Work between manufacturing and design engineers, machinists, technicians, and quality to ensure processes are robust and any production problems are quickly solved.

• Partner with design to identify and implement design for manufacturing (DFM) updates at both the piece part and system level, own change management into production.

• Aggressively implement machining process controls that allow parts to run ‘lights out’. Leverage latest technologies and programming strategies to reduce in-cycle intervention.

• Be responsible for part or part family quality; understand quality landscape, and drive projects to ensure dimensions meet part requirements with low overhead.

• Drive machining processes toward statistically controlled (SPC) environment. Develop and implement tools needed to show capability.

• Oversee full circle machining process from fixture design and manufacturing, CAM programming and program refinement, cutting tool selection, and buyoff/inspection methodologies.

• Constantly challenge each process, part, operation to create the most manufacturable and reliable engine hardware possible.

• Work with production to ensure the hardware you are responsible for is delivered on time or ahead of schedule.

• Oversee introduction and implementation of new products and products revisions, frequently multiple at a given time.

 BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: 

• Bachelor's degree in engineering discipline or physics.

• 1+ years of experience in a manufacturing environment (student project team and internship experience qualifies).

 PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: 

• Strong experience with machining concepts, problems and producing hardware.

• Ability and desire to work in a fast-paced, problem-solving environment.

• Experience in design or product development engineering role.

• Master's degree in mechanical, manufacturing, or aerospace engineering.

• Ability to work on multiple projects and initiatives in parallel.

• Mechanical component and/or tooling design and analysis (3D computer-aided design).

• Experience with process development from R&D to volume manufacturing.

• Experience writing work instructions and procedures for critical aerospace parts.

• Experience in a production environment within the aerospace industry.

 ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: 

• This is a hands-on position that will require standing for long durations of your day and working directly with hardware on the floor.

• Must be comfortable stooping, bending, and standing.

• Position may require occasional travel, long hours or weekend work.

 COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS: 

Pay Range:

Level 1: $100,000 - $117,500
Level 2: $115,000 - $140,000

 Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees accrue paid sick leave pursuant to Company policy which satisfies or exceeds the accrual, carryover, and use requirements of the law.

jobs.title: 3rd Shift - Manufacturing Engineer - Engine Assembly
jobs.desc:
Job Description Summary 
As Engine Assembly Manufacturing Engineer, you will provide on-shift manufacturing engineering support for engine assembly operations during 3rd shift, helping production teams safely build engines to quality, delivery, and cost targets. You will work directly with assemblers, technicians, quality, and support teams to resolve shop-floor issues, maintain process control, troubleshoot technical and hardware-related problems, and ensure work is performed to engineering and process requirements. You will support ongoing production by responding to disruptions, clarifying technical instructions, interpreting drawings and specifications, and making decisions within established procedures to keep assembly flowing.

This role is responsible for monitoring assembly processes, identifying and preventing defects or escapes, supporting root cause investigation and corrective actions, and driving practical process improvements that improve safety, quality, and productivity. The engineer must be able to balance immediate production needs with longer-term process discipline, communicate clearly across functions, and escalate issues that fall outside standard limits. On 3rd shift, this often means serving as a key technical resource for the operation with greater independence and ownership in real-time problem solving. 

 Job Description 
 Shift / Schedule Expectations 
 • This position supports 3rd shift operations 
• Typical hours are 10:30 pm-7:30 am 
• Regular onsite support is required during assigned shift
• May require overtime, weekend support, or schedule flexibility based on production needs
• Requires effective communication with 1st and 2nd shift teams to support shift handoff and issue continuity

 Roles and Responsibilities 
 • Provide daily manufacturing engineering support for engine assembly operations on 3rd shift
• Support assembly processes by resolving technical issues, process constraints, tooling issues, nonconformances, and build interruptions
• Work directly with assembly technicians and operators on the shop floor to troubleshoot problems and implement practical solutions
• Interpret and apply engineering drawings, specifications, work instructions, process sheets, torque requirements, fits/clearances, and assembly sequencing requirements
• Develop, revise, and improve manufacturing processes, standard work, tooling, and production documentation
• Drive improvements in safety, quality, delivery, and cost
• Lead or support root cause investigations, corrective actions, and escape prevention related to assembly defects or process variation
• Partner with quality and operations to ensure compliance with engine assembly requirements, inspection requirements, and controlled process standards
• Support implementation of lean manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives such as waste reduction, cycle time improvement, process simplification, and error-proofing
• Evaluate manufacturability and process risks and escalate issues when product or process integrity may be impacted
• Support new product introduction, process changes, tool changes, and production readiness activities as needed
• Communicate clearly across shifts and functions to ensure continuity of operations and effective issue resolution
• Use sound judgment to make timely decisions within established engineering and quality requirements, while escalating higher-risk issues appropriately

 Required Qualifications 
 • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in Engineering, Engineering Technology, Manufacturing, Mechanical, Aerospace, or related technical field ( OR High school diploma / GED with at least 4 years of relevant experience in manufacturing, mechanical assembly, aircraft maintenance, engine assembly, engine overhaul/repair, aerospace production, or other closely related technical field)

 Desired Characteristics 
 • Strong working knowledge of: • Blueprint reading and engineering drawing interpretation
• GD&T
• Tooling, fixtures, torque tools, precision measurement, and mechanical assembly methods
• Process control and configuration control
• Root cause problem solving and corrective action
• Quality requirements, defect prevention, and escape prevention
• Standard work and lean manufacturing principles

• Experience with nonconformance disposition support, inspection findings, rework processes, and deviation management
• Familiarity with manufacturing documentation, routers, work instructions, process sheets, and revision-controlled technical data
• Experience collaborating with shop operations, quality, and design engineering to resolve build issues
• Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced production environment and make decisions with urgency and discipline
• Strong communication skills and ability to work respectfully with technicians, mechanics, and cross-functional teams
 • Hands-on, practical mindset with strong shop-floor engagement
• Able to connect engineering requirements to real-world assembly execution
• Strong mechanical aptitude and product knowledge
• Effective at troubleshooting and resolving problems under production pressure
• Respectful, collaborative, and willing to learn from experienced technicians and operators
• Clear communicator who shares information across teams and shifts
• Continuous improvement mindset with a focus on safety, quality, and delivery
• High integrity, sound judgment, and disciplined decision-making in a regulated aerospace environment

 The base pay range for this position is $92,000-$105,000. The specific pay offered may be influenced by a variety of factors, including the candidate’s experience, education, and skill set. This position is also eligible for an annual discretionary bonus based on a percentage of your base salary/ commission based on the plan.  This posting is expected to close on November 1, 2026.

jobs.desc:
Job descriptions may display in multiple languages   based on your language selection. 

 What we offer: 
 At Magna, you can expect an engaging and dynamic environment where you can help to develop industry-leading automotive technologies. We invest in our employees, providing them with the support and resources they need to succeed. As a member of our global team, you can expect exciting, varied responsibilities as well as a wide range of development prospects. Because we believe that your career path should be as unique as you are.

 Group Summary: 
 As an engineering and manufacturing partner, Magna’s Complete Vehicle group helps traditional OEMs and new entrants to bring their automotive visions to life. At Magna, you will work in an innovative, international and dynamic team, always pursuing the goal of delivering high-quality products. We work in a diverse environment with global development opportunities. Together with our employees we constantly strive to create a better world of mobility.

 Job Responsibilities: 

 The Manufacturing Engineer will enhance and optimize manufacturing processes to improve efficiency, quality, and cost-effectiveness. This role involves defining and implementing change processes, managing fixtures, utilizing Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), and programming and maintaining tools. The Manufacturing Engineer will lead continuous improvement initiatives, ensure seamless implementation of process changes, and support future projects by setting up lines, ensuring station readiness, and installing equipment. Additionally, the engineer will provide critical support during production startups and ongoing production operations to ensure smooth and efficient manufacturing processes. Complete ownership and clear communication are key to succeeding in this role. The goal is to ensure that manufacturing operations run smoothly, efficiently, and safely, while meeting production targets and maintaining high standards of quality.   

 Key Responsibilities 

 • Develop, implement, and maintain manufacturing processes to improve efficiency, quality, and cost-effectiveness. 
• Analyze current manufacturing processes and identify areas for improvement. 
• Define and document change processes, ensuring all modifications are systematically recorded and communicated. 
• Lead line balancing activities as needed according to production needs and improvements. 
• Provide all required equipment and tools in all areas by analyzing the need and requirement. 
• Integrate and optimize the use of Atlas Copco tools within the manufacturing process. 
• Ensure tools are properly maintained, calibrated, and used according to manufacturer specifications. 
• Program Atlas Copco tools according to process needs to ensure optimal performance and accuracy. 
• Provide training and support to production staff on the proper use of Atlas Copco tools. 
• Lead responsibilities for line setup, station readiness, and equipment installations for future projects. 
• Ensure all new setups and installations meet operational requirements and safety standards. 
• Coordinate with relevant teams to ensure timely and efficient project execution. 
• Order fixtures according to CAD specifications and ensure timely validation upon arrival. 
• Maintain and replace fixtures as needed to meet production requirements. 
• Collaborate with vendors to design and manufacture new fixtures when necessary, ensuring they meet operational needs and safety standards. 
• Ensure fixtures are properly maintained and calibrated. 
• Analyze proposed changes and provide detailed assessments of cost, process, and time impact within the timeframe given by the change coordinator. 
• Lead the implementation of approved changes in the process without disrupting production. 
• Work cross-functionally with IT, Supply Chain Management (SCM), and Quality teams to implement changes. 
• Clearly communicate throughout the change process to ensure all stakeholders are informed and aligned. 
• Lead and participate in continuous improvement initiatives to enhance manufacturing processes. 
• Conduct root cause analysis and implement corrective actions to resolve production issues.  
• Work closely with cross-functional teams, including production, quality, commissioning, rework and maintenance, to ensure seamless integration of process improvements. 
• Communicate effectively with all levels of the organization to ensure alignment and understanding of process changes.

jobs.desc:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE JOB

 We are looking for an Industrial Engineer to join our rapidly growing team in Quonset, RI. This role sits within our technical shared services organization (3SI) and carries a dual mandate. First, you operate as a flexible resource for the site: production lines "lease" your time to design and optimize their manufacturing operations as their needs peak and shift — moving across programs and bringing data-driven IE rigor to production line and workstation design, capital equipment, and the metrics that keep a line healthy. Second, you hold a standing factory-macro remit on behalf of 3SI: owning site-level factory layouts, leading cross-functional technical projects, and optimizing material flow across the whole facility rather than any single line. You'll zoom from one line's workstation up to how the entire site moves material and uses its floor space, working shoulder-to-shoulder with Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, Business Operations, and the Factory Services team to get complex undersea hardware built and shipped to spec.

If you are someone who thrives on bringing order to a fast-scaling production floor — and can hold both the single-line detail and the whole-factory picture at once — this role is for you.

 WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Deliver core Industrial Engineering standards and capabilities to Quonset's production lines — capacity planning, labor standards, time studies, workstation and line layouts, and discrete event simulation (DES)

• Deploy across production lines as a shared resource — partnering with each line's Manufacturing leads to scope the work, deliver it, and hand off cleanly

• Own site-level factory layout and material flow — plan and maintain the master floor layout and optimize how material moves between receiving, storage, lineside, and shared services as programs scale and new capabilities come online

• Specify, justify, and deploy capital equipment and tooling — define requirements, own the business case and capex justification, and support vendor selection, build, install, and qualification through to production readiness.

• Lead cross-functional technical projects on behalf of 3SI — scope, schedule, and drive site infrastructure, equipment, and process-improvement initiatives from definition through execution.

• Own operations health metrics and KPIs and build the tools and reports that communicate line and site health across the org.

• Identify bottlenecks and constraints across layout, part shortages, staffing, and tooling, then drive resolution with Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Engineering, and Quality.

 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• 5+ years past experience in a rate manufacturing environment and production-type role where complex mechanical and/or electrical assemblies were built.

• Experience using real operational data to make informed suggestions and decisions.

• Experience and demonstrated skills with AutoCAD.

• Proven line/facility design: value stream mapping, continuous/one-piece flow, and workstation design

• Experience with Lean Manufacturing principles/implementation.

• Able to read technical documentation (drawings, vendor schematics, CAD) and understand hardware processes across electronics and mechanical structures

• Understanding of the means and methods of how material flows around a facility including but not limited to pull systems + triggers, Kanban and MIN MAX calculations.

• Experience modeling operations using discrete event simulation.

• Working knowledge of an MES and an ERP (Oracle or equivalent).

• Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Bachelor's or higher in Industrial, Mechanical, Aerospace, Manufacturing, Electrical, or Computer Engineering.

• Hands-on design of tooling, fixtures, or GSE (ground support equipment) for heavy or large-format hardware.

• Data analytics knowledge and experience including the use of SQL to create complex custom queries, mining and joining tables from production and supply chain databases (experience with Palantir Foundry a plus).

• Experience creating and owning program, project or production schedules.

• Experience with Simio and/or Siemen’s Plant Simulation.

• Experience in a marine, subsea, or other regulated/harsh-environment hardware program

Req ID:532288 

 À la tête des entreprises qui s’engagent vers un avenir plus vert, Alstom développe et commercialise des solutions de mobilité qui apportent les fondements durables pour l'avenir des transports. Notre portefeuille de produits s'étend des trains à grande vitesse, métros, monorails et tramways jusqu’aux systèmes intégrés, services sur mesure, infrastructures, signalisation et solutions de mobilité numérique. Nous rejoindre, c'est rejoindre une entreprise bienveillante, responsable et innovante où plus de 80 000 personnes ouvrent la voie à une mobilité plus verte et plus intelligente, dans le monde entier.
 Pourriez-vous être le Chef de Projets Bogie (H/F) à temps plein que nous recherchons au Creusot  ?

 Notre site Alstom Le Creusot (800 salariés), situé à 1h20 de Paris et à 40 min de Lyon en TGV, Centre d'excellence en matière de conception et de fabrication de bogies (châssis, roues, essieux, freins) pour les TGV, trams, trains, métros en France et dans le monde recherche un(e) Chef de Projet.

 Votre futur rôle 

 Relevez un nouveau défi et mettez à profit votre expertise en gestion de projet dans un secteur en pleine transformation. Vous travaillerez avec des équipes dynamiques, collaboratives et multidisciplinaires, et vous jouerez un rôle clé dans la réalisation de projets ferroviaires d’envergure internationale, contribuant ainsi à façonner la mobilité durable de demain.

 Au quotidien, vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec les équipes internes (planning, achats, logistique, études, industrialisation, qualité, etc.), tout en assurant la coordination avec le client final. Vous serez également impliqué(e) dans des initiatives transverses d'amélioration continue.

 Vous vous occuperez plus particulièrement de la gestion contractuelle et financière des projets, mais aussi de l’identification et de la gestion des risques et opportunités. Nous ferons appel à vous pour :

• 
 Gérer un ou plusieurs projets internationaux, de l’obtention du contrat jusqu’à la sortie de garantie.

• 
 Assurer la coordination des équipes pluridisciplinaires associées à vos projets.

• 
 Être l’interlocuteur(trice) principal(e) du client final pour le site.

• 
 Garantir le respect des délais, des budgets et des niveaux de qualité attendus.

• 
 Superviser la gestion contractuelle et financière des projets.

• 
 Identifier et exploiter les risques et opportunités liés aux projets.

• 
 Contribuer activement à des programmes transverses d’amélioration continue.

• 
 Jouer un rôle moteur dans l’atteinte des objectifs du site et du groupe.

 Votre profil 

 Nous accordons plus d'importance à la passion et à l’état d’esprit qu'à l'expérience. C'est pourquoi nous n'attendons pas de vous que vous possédiez toutes les compétences. Nous avons plutôt dressé une liste de celles qui, selon nous, vous aideront à réussir et à vous épanouir dans ce rôle :

• 
 Diplôme d’ingénieur en mécanique ou généraliste.

• 
 Expérience de 5 ans minimum en gestion de projet, idéalement dans un environnement industriel.

• 
 Compétences techniques, organisationnelles et relationnelles solides.

• 
 Esprit fédérateur et capacité à dynamiser les équipes.

• 
 Sens de l’anticipation et forte adaptabilité.

• 
 Maîtrise de l’anglais, indispensable pour ce poste.

• 
 Connaissance des outils et méthodologies de gestion de projet (un atout).

• 
 Capacité à travailler dans un environnement multiculturel et multidisciplinaire.

 Ce que vous apprécierez Rejoignez-nous pour une nouvelle expérience de vie - le secteur ferroviaire est un secteur d’avenir, vous pouvez donc vous développer et acquérir de nouvelles compétences et expériences tout au long de votre carrière. Vous pourrez également :

• 
 Bénéficier de stabilité, de défis et d'une carrière à long terme sans routine quotidienne.

• 
 Travailler avec des équipes passionnées et engagées dans la transition vers une mobilité verte.

• 
 Collaborer avec des équipes transversales et des collègues qualifiés.

• 
 Contribuer à des projets innovants et à fort impact.

• 
 Utiliser notre environnement de travail stimulant et inclusif.

• 
 Orienter votre carrière dans la direction de votre choix à travers les fonctions et les pays.

• 
 Bénéficier de notre investissement dans votre développement, par le biais de programmes d’apprentissage primés.

• 
 Progresser vers des rôles de leadership ou d’expertise technique au sein du groupe.

• 
 Bénéficier d'un système de rémunération équitable et dynamique qui reconnaît vos performances et votre potentiel, ainsi que d'une couverture sociale complète et compétitive (assurance-vie, assurance-maladie, pension).

 Il n'est pas nécessaire d'être un passionné de trains pour s'épanouir chez nous. Nous vous garantissons que lorsque vous monterez dans l'un de nos trains avec vos amis ou votre famille, vous en serez fier. Si vous êtes prêt à relever le défi, nous aimerions vous connaître !
 Important 

 En tant qu'entreprise mondiale, nous sommes un employeur qui prône l'égalité des chances et qui célèbre la diversité dans les 63 pays où nous sommes présents. Nous nous engageons à créer un lieu de travail inclusif pour tous.

jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer II, Turbomachinery
jobs.desc:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known. 

 Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us. 

 About the Team: 

 The Engine Manufacturing team is dedicated to delivering high-performance engines and advancing innovative manufacturing systems that continuously improve cost, quality, and lead time. You’re not just executing on designs; you actively provide input that shapes new hardware iterations and regularly interface with engineers to make critical decisions for the Aeon R program. Having successfully developed and refined processes for our initial development engines, the team is now focused on producing flight engines at rate for Terran R’s aggressive launch manifest. 

 About the Role: 

 As a Turbomachinery Engineer, you will produce components and assemblies for the fuel and oxidizer turbopumps of the Aeon-R and Aeon-R Vac engines. As a Propulsion Manufacturing Engineer, you will own the manufacturing trades and then develop the processes for fabricating, testing, and delivering critical Aeon-R hardware and subassemblies. You will serve as the main point-of-contact between the manufacturing and design teams as we optimize Aeon-R architecture and scale manufacturing operations. To be successful in this role, you should be someone who thrives in ambiguity and is able to drive their own projects to completion. You must have the passion, tenacity and resolve to work through challenging issues unique to rocket turbopumps and additively manufactured hardware. We are looking for someone multifaceted, and capable of working at the interfaces of design, development, and analysis of turbomachinery. Ideally, you are someone who has come from a fast paced, aerospace environment, having completed difficult projects while collaborating effectively with multidisciplinary groups. 

 About You: 

• Degree in engineering or related technical field and 2+ years of relevant experience 

• Experience with turbopump assembly procedures, including rotor balancing, interference fits, clearance checks, structural proofing, and leak checks 

• Manufacturing Process Experience: Fluids Testing, Machining, Additive 

• Knowledge of general assembly and test procedures, including tolerance stack-up analysis, structural proof testing, and pressurized leak checks 

• Experience with Siemens NX or other CAD and analysis tools 

• Experience with Tooling design, including conceptualization, modeling and drafting, and detailed analysis 

 Nice to haves but not required: 

• Experience working with additively manufactured engine hardware 

• Experience with GD&T (ASME Y14.5) and industry specifications 

• Experience in a startup or agile development environment 

• Experience working in a flight development program 

 At Relativity Space, we are committed to transparency and fairness in our compensation practices. Actual compensation will be determined based on experience, qualifications, and other job-related factors. 

 Compensation is only one part of our total rewards package. Relativity Space offers competitive salary and equity, a generous PTO and sick leave policy, parental leave, an annual learning and development stipend, and more! To see some of the benefits & perks we offer, please visit here. 

 Hiring Range:
 $104,000 — $156,000 USD 

 We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

 Company: 
The Boeing Company 

 The Boeing Test and Evaluation (BT&E) team is looking for an Associate Manufacturing Engineer to join our growing team in Berkeley, MO . The Manufacturing Engineer is an assembly and installation engineer within BT&E that supports fabrication planning & setup/installation by providing design review, manufacturing plan authorship, and fabrication sourcing (inside and outside of Boeing) followed by support at the aircraft during installation or in the laboratory during setup.  They are also expected to work closely with our in-house shop team comprised of tooling and aircraft mechanics which support our operations.

jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer, Altius
jobs.desc:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE TEAM

 The Launched Effects team at Anduril is responsible for scaling the manufacturing and delivery of the Altius family of systems (including the ALTIUS-600 and ALTIUS-700). As the premier Air-Launched Effects (ALE) platform for the U.S. military and its allies, ALTIUS is redefining modern warfare. These tube-launched, autonomous aerial systems must be built to survive extreme deployment environments, requiring precision manufacturing of advanced composites, complex avionics, and modular payload integrations for ISR, Electronic Warfare, and kinetic strike capabilities.

As part of the Launched Effects manufacturing team, you will bridge the gap between cutting-edge R&D and high-rate production. We are a fast-moving, mission-driven group of manufacturing engineers, quality specialists, and production operations experts who refuse to accept traditional, slow defense manufacturing timelines. We continuously optimize our assembly lines, implement automated testing, design for manufacturing (DFM), and build resilient supply chains to deploy reliable systems to the front lines at unprecedented speed. If you want to work on a team where your production and manufacturing decisions directly impact global security, this is it.

 ABOUT THE JOB

 This role is about much more than just processes; it's about orchestrating the industrialization of a vital product. You will own the entire manufacturing value-chain for Altius, from current rate to high-volume deployment. Your responsibilities will span the spectrum: driving Design for Manufacturability (DFM) feedback into design, innovating tool design and selection, creating and optimizing high-rate production lines, fostering strategic vendor partnerships, embedding robust quality assurance throughout, and meticulously documenting build processes.

 *This position is permanently based in Ashville, OH , and requires candidates to temporarily relocate for a comprehensive 3-month training program: 1 month in Santa Ana, CA , followed by 2 months (approximately) in Atlanta, GA . To support your transition, Anduril will fully provide and cover all corporate housing, transportation, and travel accommodations during this training period. Your recruiter will discuss the logistics of this program with you in detail during the hiring process 

 WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Execute the manufacturing of a certain product or set of products, from initial prototyping through large full-scale production.

• Work with design engineers during the development process to drive design for manufacturing best practices into the design effort, and help facilitate the transition from design to prototype to rate production.

• Act as a manufacturing laison for mechanical fabrication and avionics with subject matter expertise in these areas and key experience in design for manufacturability.

• Own documentation required for successfully manufacturing product group hardware at scale, such as MBOM’s, work instructions & requirements, etc.

• Advise on quality management and business application programs as they pertain to manufacturing within your area.

• Collaborate with internal customers and manufacturing planning teams to define capacity planning actions to meet customer needs and expectations.

• Analyze metrics for continuous improvement initiatives (cost reduction, QI reduction & capacity increase).

• Instill a culture of innovation, teamwork, and accountability within the manufacturing engineering product team.

• Develop production and test methodologies and implement best practices to enable scaling production capabilities for larger, more complex products.

• Travel to suppliers and partner sites to do initial sourcing work, solve ongoing production issues, and implement process procedures as required.

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams, which requires regular interaction with production and manufacturing stakeholders and frequently working directly on the production floor.

 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Degree in a technical field preferred such as engineering, math, or a hard science.

• 2+ years of experience in a relevant field, preferably manufacturing or design of electromechanical hardware.

• Demonstrated ability to creatively deliver electromechanical hardware in a resource-constrained environment.

• An attitude of world-class mission assurance, quality, attention to detail, and dedication.

• A genuine interest in manufacturing and thirst for learning.

• Candidates must demonstrate flexibility and dedication, being prepared to work extended hours and weekends when dictated by critical business priorities.

• Regular travel between our various locations is an essential component of this role.

• U.S. citizenship is required pursuant to contractual obligations.

 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Exposure to aircraft programs or other relevant aerospace & defense technologies.

• Software scripting experience in any language.

• Lean Six Sigma certification (Green Belt or higher) or equivalent experience.

• Familiarity with J-STD-001, IPC-A-610, and IPC/WHMA-A-620 or equivalent standards.

jobs.title: Senior Manufacturing Engineer, Maritime Systems
jobs.desc:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE TEAM

 Anduril’s Manufacturing Technology, Maritime Team is seeking a Senior Manufacturing Engineer, Maritime Systems. The Maritime Manufacturing Technology Team is responsible for rapidly developing and implementing manufacturing technologies and processes for cutting-edge defense hardware, including deployable static and moving surface, undersea and sea to air vehicles and scaling these products in our new manufacturing facilities.

 ABOUT THE JOB

 As a Senior Manufacturing Engineer, you will own the critical bridge between engineering design and full-rate production for our advanced autonomous systems. This role is a hybrid of manufacturing process development and manufacturing planning, requiring you to design and validate how we build our hardware while also creating the detailed plans and documentation to execute it at scale. You will develop and implement robust manufacturing processes that are efficient, repeatable, and compliant with rigorous customer requirements, including those specified by NAVSEA, enabling the delivery of mission-critical capabilities.

 WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Manufacturing Process: Design, develop, and qualify robust manufacturing processes for complex maritime systems, from component fabrication and sub-assembly through final vehicle integration and testing.

• Manufacturing Planning: Author and maintain comprehensive manufacturing plans, translate complex 2D/3D engineering drawings into clear work instructions, and create optimized process routings in our MES (Forge).

• Own the creation and maintenance of the Manufacturing Bill of Materials (MBOM), ensuring accurate translation from the Engineering Bill of Materials (EBOM) and meticulously documenting the as-built configuration.

• Lead Design for Manufacturability (DFM) and producibility assessments, providing critical, data-driven feedback to the design team to optimize for cost, quality, and scalability.

• Identify, specify, and qualify all tooling, fixtures, and test equipment required to support manufacturing and assembly operations in accordance with program requirements.

• Drive continuous improvement by leading process validation activities, applying statistical methods, and performing root cause analysis to resolve manufacturing discrepancies and enhance production efficiency.

• Serve as the primary technical interface between design engineering, supply chain, and production operations, ensuring alignment and resolving issues to meet delivery commitments.

• Provide hands-on, on-floor engineering support during new product introduction (NPI), critical build phases, and troubleshooting activities.

 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• 5+ years of experience as a Manufacturing Engineer, with a demonstrated background in both manufacturing process development and production planning.

• Proven experience in a New Product Introduction (NPI) environment, successfully taking complex products from design into a production environment.

• Strong technical understanding of manufacturing processes and techniques (e.g., mechanical assembly, electrical integration, composite fabrication, precision machining).

• Proficiency in reading and interpreting complex engineering drawings and technical specifications, including an understanding of GD&T.

• Hands-on experience with Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES) and Product Data Management (PDM) software.

• Ability to thrive and communicate effectively in a fast-paced, rapidly scaling R&D and production environment.

• Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Bachelor's degree in Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

• Direct experience in the maritime, naval, or aerospace defense industry, with an understanding of associated quality and documentation standards (e.g., NAVSEA, MIL-SPEC).

• Experience with Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems for material and production planning.

• Background in process characterization, statistical process control (SPC), and designing/qualifying automated manufacturing and test equipment.

• Experience leading cross-functional teams to resolve complex manufacturing challenges.

jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer
jobs.desc:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE TEAM

 The Anduril Battlespace Awareness Radar team develops state-of-the-art radar systems to tackle significant security challenges for America and its allies. The team is seeking an RF Manufacturing Engineer to help bridge the gap between radar hardware design and scalable production. They are responsible for all aspects of radar system development, from ideation through initial production. In this role, you will work closely with interdisciplinary technical teams — including RF engineers, systems engineers, and operations — to develop and optimize manufacturing processes for complex RF and electronic assemblies, ensuring radar systems transition smoothly from prototype to full-rate production.

 WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Own the development and optimization of manufacturing processes for RF electronic assemblies, from initial prototyping through transition to full production.

• Develop and maintain manufacturing process documentation including assembly instructions, workflow/routing, inspection plans, and tool and fixture designs for RF hardware and electronic subassemblies.

• Troubleshoot complex electrical and RF manufacturing issues on the production line, applying root cause analysis and corrective action methodologies to permanently resolve problems.

• Drive continuous improvement of manufacturing processes through data analysis, process capability studies, and application of best practices to improve yield, reduce cycle time, and decrease cost.

• Support design-for-manufacturability efforts by providing real-time feedback to RF and electrical design engineers on producibility, component selection, and assembly constraints.

• Develop and validate test procedures and fixtures for electronic products, components, and RF systems to ensure production quality and performance.

• Collaborate cross-functionally with design engineering, quality, supply chain, and operations teams to support new product introductions with accelerated time to market.

• Support critical customer-facing hardware demonstrations and use these interactions to better understand manufacturing requirements and end-user needs.

• Travel to test sites, supplier facilities, or partner locations as needed.

 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• BS in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, or a related engineering field

• 3+ years of engineering experience in an electronics or RF hardware production environment

• Familiarity with RF Test Software such as Keysight IO library suite (BenchVue), NIMAX or equivalent

• Demonstrated experience with manufacturing processes for electronic assemblies, including SMT, soldering (J-STD-001 or equivalent), and board-level integration

• Ability to interpret complex engineering drawings, schematics and RF-specific specifications

• Hands-on troubleshooting skills with electronic and RF hardware, including the use of test equipment such as network analyzers, signal & spectrum analyzers, and oscilloscopes

• Strong problem-solving skills with experience applying root cause/corrective action (RCCA) or similar structured methodologies

• Excellent communication skills and ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, cross-functional team environment

• Eligible to obtain and maintain an active Secret clearance

 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Experience with RF design principals and RF-specific manufacturing processes such as waveguide assembly, antenna array fabrication, microwave component integration, or radar T/R module production

• Experience with RF and Antenna testing such as S-parameter characterization and antenna pattern measurement

• Familiarity with manufacturing execution systems (MES), SAP, or similar production management tools

• Experience with ECAD tools (e.g., Altium) for reviewing designs, troubleshooting issues and developing tooling/fixtures

• Experience interfacing with RF test equipment through manufacturer protocols (eg SCPI, GPIB, etc)

• Experience with programming or scripting (e.g., Python, VBA, SQL,) for process automation and data analysis

• Knowledge of EMI/EMC constraints and their impact on manufacturing and assembly processes

• Experience supporting the manufacture of complex electronic systems for defense or aerospace applications

• Experience leading or mentoring junior manufacturing engineers

jobs.title: Senior Vehicle Structures Design Engineer
jobs.desc:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known. 

 Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us. 

 About the Team: 

 The Structures and Mechanisms team is responsible for the full design, build, and test lifecycle of Terran R’s integrated structures and flight mechanisms. Whether you're working on highly iterative mechanisms that move or tight-margin structures that shouldn’t, you’ll get hands-on hardware ownership and see the rocket coming to life on the factory floor. Both teams fall under one department, sharing design principles, tools, and an integrated approach that provides a comprehensive view of Terran R. Team members work on multiple parts, not just within a single subsystem, and are empowered to make decisions that directly impact flight hardware. Beyond first flight, you’ll play a critical role in refining for manufacturability and speed. 

 About the Role: 

• The scope of work encompasses designing parts and systems from early conceptualization through full release and supporting manufacturing for primary and secondary structures related to all stages of the Terran R rocket. You will need to think creatively and leverage innovation to optimize part geometry, ensure assembly packaging, prevent interferences and excessive gapping, reduce mass, and make parts fully manufacturable. You’ll also assist manage parts and assemblies throughout their lifecycles in PLM, and you’ll control BOM structuring and configuration management for many systems across the vehicle. 

• Your responsibilities will include, but not be limited to the following: 

• Design and develop piece parts, assemblies, and systems from early conceptualization up through full initial release – working with large machined metallic components, sheet metal, composites, formed panels, and more 

• Integrate critical design for manufacturing choices in direct coordination with the manufacturing engineering team 

• Perform packaging assessment of systems – resolve interferences, perform tolerance stack analyses, validate hardware stacks and fastener selections, integrate nominal gapping and shimming strategies, and more 

• Support BOM and configuration management of various systems across multiple vehicles 

• Create and release drawings as part of system release sprints post-CDR, including incorporating GD&T as primary definition In order to be successful in this role, you must be someone who is self-motivated, adaptable and is able to lead your own projects to completion in a fast-paced environment. Ideally, you have significant mechanical or structural design experience and a proven track record completing collaborative projects effectively. 

• On a weekly basis, you will be designing flight components for our upcoming Terran R vehicle using NX/TeamCenter, creating and releasing drawings as well as supporting fabrication of your components. You will also use your strong organizational skills to properly document your work and present your recommendations when decisions are needed. 

 About You: 

• 4+ years of experience in a design engineering role 

• Bachelor’s degree in engineering or related discipline 

• Experience with industry-standard CAD packages such as NX, CATIA, Creo, or SOLIDWORKS 

• Fundamental knowledge of structures strength, stability and fatigue failure mechanisms 

• Ability to work in the context of large assemblies and effectively navigate large vehicle BOM’s 

 Nice to haves but not required: 

• 2+ years experience with NX/Teamcenter PLM 

• 3+ years experience with GD&T and drafting 

 At Relativity Space, we are committed to transparency and fairness in our compensation practices. Actual compensation will be determined based on experience, qualifications, and other job-related factors. 

 Compensation is only one part of our total rewards package. Relativity Space offers competitive salary and equity, a generous PTO and sick leave policy, parental leave, an annual learning and development stipend, and more! To see some of the benefits & perks we offer, please visit here.

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE TEAM

 Anduril’s Manufacturing team is seeking a Manufacturing Engineer to join our team. The Manufacturing Team is responsible for rapidly iterating and building cutting-edge defense hardware, including static equipment, moving ground equipment, and flight vehicles. This responsibility includes everything in the manufacturing value-chain, including, but not limited to, Design for Manufacturability work, tool design & selection, process creation & optimization, vendor sourcing & interaction, quality planning, and work documentation associated with the hardware that the Manufacturing Engineer owns.

 The right person for this role can demonstrate past holistic ownership on solving a technical challenge with a creative, physical, solution that they either personally manufacturing or oversaw manufacturing on, in a fast-paced, resource-limited environment. If you are someone who thrives in such an environment, then this role is for you. 

 WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Own a portion or all of the manufacturing value chain for a certain product or set of products

• Develop novel tooling solutions for fabrication and assembly of structural parts

• Develop process flows, breaking down large, complex assemblies into a logical part flow of subassemblies and sub-processes

• Write documentation required for successfully manufacturing their hardware at scale, such as work instructions, quality plans, inspection requirements, etc.

• Work with contract manufacturers across various disciplines (PCBA fab, metallic manufacturing, assembly, etc.) to develop repeatable, sustained processes for quick-turn development as well as at-scale production

• Work with technicians and other engineers hands-on, building prototype hardware

• Contribute to end-customer hardware mechanical or electrical design, including interconnects, board fabrication and inspection, etc.

• Travel to suppliers to do initial sourcing work, solve ongoing production issues, and implement quality procedures

 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Degree in a technical field such as engineering, math, or a hard science

• 2+ years of experience in a relevant field, preferably manufacturing or design of electromechanical hardware

• Demonstrated ability to creatively deliver electromechanical hardware in a resource-constrained environment

• Demonstrated in-kind or direct team leadership skills, with backing examples

• Personal experience physically manufacturing hardware via any means (machining, fabrication, soldering, assembly, etc.) Work on personal or extracurricular projects is a plus.

• A genuine interest in manufacturing and thirst for learning

• U.S. Person status is required as this position needs to access export controlled data

 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• PCBA fabrication experience including prior work with or setup/modification/monitoring SMT processes

• Hands-on experience with R/C and/or autonomous flight vehicles, flight controllers, or other related control systems

• Software scripting experience in any language

 Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

 Manufacturing Engineering powers Rocket Lab's factories from concept to full-scale production. We're seeking Manufacturing Engineers across multiple disciplines to turn early ideas into manufacturable designs, build and optimize the systems that make them real, and constantly push for faster, better, smarter ways to build rockets.

 THE OPPORTUNITIES: 

 We're hiring across four key manufacturing disciplines:

• Assembly & Integration   – Mechanical, Assembly, Propulsion, Mechanical Test

• Avionics & Test   – Electronics manufacturing, electrical test, debugging systems

• Composites  – Advanced materials, resins, ablatives, sandwich structures

• Machining  – CNC programming, precision manufacturing, GD&T

 In your application, please indicate which discipline(s) align with your experience and interests. 

 YOU'LL GET TO: 

• Own & Ship: 

• Become the expert on products you help build and launch

• Help teams hit production goals while maintaining quality

• Improve existing products and support new designs

• Solve & Fix: 

• Investigate why things fail and implement fixes

• Make calls on whether parts meet flight standards using engineering analysis

• Connect production, quality, and design teams to solve problems fast

• Build & Improve: 

• Write clear procedures so production runs smoothly every time

• Design reliable hardware and test setups

• Create test methods for critical systems

• Use Lean/Six Sigma to make things better and faster

• Lead & Scale: 

• Review designs to make sure they're easy to build and test

• Help launch new products to the factory floor

• Identify equipment needs and build the business case

• Set up better systems for planning, quality tracking, and data

• Grow & Deliver: 

• Mentor technicians and newer engineers

• Break big projects into manageable pieces and ship them

• Run your own projects with minimal oversight

• Document wins and lessons learned for the team

 YOU'LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS: 

 Core requirements (all disciplines): 

• Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Mechatronics, Computer Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Material Science, or similar

• 0-5 years of technical experience in a Manufacturing, Production, or Process Engineering environment

• Hands-on experience solving problems in complex manufacturing systems

• Ability to effectively deliver on complex assignments with autonomy

• Foundational knowledge in complex manufacturing processes

• Strong communication skills, both written and verbal

• Can-do approach and flexibility to thrive in a fast-paced, evolving environment

 Additional discipline-specific experience (one or more of): 

• Avionics & Test:  Debugging electro-mechanical systems, understanding of instrumentation and sensors

• Composites:  Knowledge of advanced composites materials, tooling, and manufacturing processes

• Machining:   GD&T and inspection methods, CAM software for 3 and 5-axis CNC machines, 2+ years machine shop experience

• Assembly & Integration:  Experience with mechanical assembly, integration, or test processes

 BONUS POINTS FOR: 

• Experience in aerospace, defense, or high-reliability manufacturing

• Lean manufacturing or Six Sigma knowledge

• Cross-discipline manufacturing exposure

• Experience with ERP/PLM Systems (Siemens Team Center, Infor LN)

• Knowledge of production quality metrics

• Experience with environmental and production acceptance testing (vibration, shock, thermal, vacuum)

• Understanding of instrumentation, interfaces, and sensors (power supplies, oscilloscopes, serial devices, accelerometers, thermocouples, RTDs, 4-20mA sensors)

 EXPECTATIONS 

• Provide solutions and ideas when faced with engineering challenges

• Share knowledge on effectiveness of theories and concepts

• Navigate and complete daily tasks within technical systems

• Create and improve technical documentation

• Communicate effectively with peers and contribute to team objectives

• Demonstrate professionalism, punctuality, and adherence to company policies

• Ensure health and safety policies and procedures are followed at all times

 ADDITIONAL INFORMATION 

• Domestic and international travel may be required

• Additional duties as reasonably required

• Adherence to company policies and procedures is expected

 WHAT TO EXPECT 

 We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

 MANUFACTURING ENGINEER (FALCON & DRAGON) 

 As a Manufacturing Engineer at SpaceX, you will have the opportunity to utilize your knowledge, experience, and creativity to develop novel solutions at the cutting edge of space technology. You will work on launch vehicles and spacecraft that deliver satellites into Earth's orbit, ferry humans to and from the International Space Station, and ultimately extend humanity’s reach beyond the Earth and moon. You will be a vital part of the relationship between our development and production teams. You will provide input into the design and development of new and existing hardware and take a lead role in manufacturing and integration on our current and next-generation vehicles.

 RESPONSIBILITIES: 

• Responsible for the build and inspection process for the structural assembly, propulsion assembly, and integration of the Falcon & Dragon vehicles

• Develop, qualify, and refine manufacturing processes to meet all design and business requirements, including safety, quality, efficiency, and delivery

• Collaborate with other engineers, subject matter experts, and technicians to solve large-scale production challenges

• Work with design engineers to evaluate designs for manufacturability and implementation in a rapidly evolving production environment

• Resolve product non-conformances and collaborate with the quality team to implement root cause corrective actions

• Identify, plan, and execute capital equipment, machine, and layout upgrades to meet volume production demand

• Develop and refine floor layouts, capacity models, and product flow analysis to ensure on-time vehicle delivery to manifest

 BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: 

• Bachelor's degree in mechanical, manufacturing, aerospace, materials or industrial engineering

• 1+ years of engineering experience in manufacturing or production (internship and school projects experience qualifies)

 PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: 

• Master’s degree in mechanical, manufacturing, aerospace, materials or industrial engineering

• Involvement in a professional engineering society or collegiate design project

• Experience with the build, assembly, or integration of large mechanical assemblies

• Knowledge of metallic manufacturing techniques, processes, and equipment related to welding, metal forming, fastening, drilling, bonding and automation

• Mechanical component and/or tooling design and analysis experience using 3D CAD software

• Experience with design for manufacture and assembly (DFMA)

• Experience transition complex products from R&D to high-volume manufacturing in a fast-paced environment

• Experience writing work instructions and procedures for critical aerospace parts

• Experience in a production environment within the aerospace industry

 ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: 

• Willing to work extended hours and/or weekends as needed

 COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS: 

Pay range: 
Manufacturing Engineer/Level I: $100,000.00 - $117,500.00/per year 
Manufacturing Engineer/Level II: $115,000.00 - $140,000.00/per year 

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Job Summary

 Manufacturing Engineer | Greenfield Mfg. Launch / Process Readiness:

 The Manufacturing Engineer will be responsible for developing, validating, and launching manufacturing processes for a large-scale greenfield manufacturing facility .  This role supports the end-to-end industrialization journey from early process planning through equipment installation, commissioning, production ramp-up, and operational handovers.
The role focuses on translating products, process, quality, safety, capacity, and business requirements into capable, repeatable, scalable, and efficient manufacturing systems. The ideal candidate will combine strong manufacturing engineering fundamentals, hands-on shop-floor experience, and cross-functional leadership to support large-scale factory launch and ramp-up.

 Key Responsibilities

• Lead manufacturing process development from concept planning through production launch and ramp-up.

• Define production line requirements, workstation concepts, tooling and fixture needs, equipment interfaces, labor assumptions, process flows, and manufacturing documentation.

• Partner with Product Engineering, Operations, Quality, Equipment Engineering, Controls Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Layout Engineering, Supply Chain, Facilities, Construction, EHS, and Maintenance teams to integrate manufacturing requirements into the overall plant design.

• Provide manufacturing inputs to factory master planning, including line layout, equipment placement, operator movement, material presentation, utility needs, ergonomics, safety, maintainability, and scalability.

• Participate in design reviews and provide DFM/DFA feedback to improve manufacturability, assembly efficiency, serviceability, quality, and cost.

• Support equipment installation, commissioning, debug, process validation, run-at-rate, ramp-up stabilization, and transition to stable operations.

• Analyze production performance using OEE, cycle time, downtime, yield, scrap, rework, labor utilization, first-time quality, defect trends, and throughput data.

• Strong ownership mindset with focus on safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, and scalability.

• Systems-thinking mindset with strong attention to detail.
